title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a transmon qubit, and an NV center ensemble, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe a characteristic three-mode avoided crossing, indicating strong coupling between all three components, and extract coupling strengths and cooperativities.
conclusion: This work establishes a solid-state platform for coherent interactions between superconducting circuits and spin ensembles, enabling future quantum networking and transduction applications.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases that are not well understood experimentally.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting quantum processor, the authors implement a quantum circuit with repeated measurements and conditional feedback, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement entropy.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, controlled by the measurement rate and feedback strength, consistent with theoretical predictions for monitored quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used to engineer nonequilibrium phases of matter, providing a platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and information processing in open systems.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in classical systems; its quantum counterpart is of fundamental interest in non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states with different temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics.
result: They observe the quantum Mpemba effect, where initially hotter states relax faster, and demonstrate modulation of the effect by controlling system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of the quantum Mpemba effect and opens avenues for controlling relaxation dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Probing Quantum States Over Spacetime Through Interferometry
authors: Seok Hyung Lie And Hyukjoon Kwon
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie and Hyukjoon Kwon

Establishing a notion of the quantum state that applies consistently across space and time could be a crucial step toward formulating a relativistic quantum theory. We give an operational meaning to multipartite quantum states over arbitrary regions in spacetime through a causally agnostic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a causally agnostic measurement framework to operationally define multipartite quantum states over arbitrary spacetime regions, bridging quantum information and relativistic quantum theory.
motivation: Establishing a consistent notion of quantum states across spacetime is crucial for formulating a relativistic quantum theory, but current approaches lack operational meaning for states defined on arbitrary spacetime regions.
method: The authors develop a causally agnostic measurement scheme that assigns a quantum state to any spacetime region based on interferometric measurements, without assuming a preferred causal structure.
result: They show that the resulting state is well-defined and satisfies consistency conditions, enabling the probing of quantum correlations across spacelike and timelike separations.
conclusion: This work provides an operational foundation for quantum states in spacetime, potentially impacting quantum information processing in relativistic settings and tests of quantum gravity.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and estimates entropy production.
motivation: To experimentally observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven optical system, linking stochastic switching to entropy production.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and thermodynamic irreversibility, with quantified entropy production.
conclusion: Optical bistability provides a platform to study non-equilibrium thermodynamics and irreversible dynamics in photonic systems.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, and quantum resonators serve as versatile working fluids.
method: The authors employ a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator, analyzing fluctuations and efficiency.
result: They derive exact expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and trade-offs between power and efficiency.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum thermodynamics by providing a detailed characterization of fluctuations in a driven quantum system, with implications for quantum heat engine design.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for Petz f-divergences, linking distinguishability to quadratic contrasts.
motivation: To generalize thermodynamic uncertainty relations to a broad class of quantum divergences, providing a unified information-theoretic bound.
method: Uses operator convex functions and the Petz f-divergence framework to represent distinguishability as a mixture of quadratic contrasts.
result: Any Petz f-divergence can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, leading to a universal uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental link between quantum information measures and thermodynamic constraints, with implications for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks; nonreciprocal elements offer a way to route quantum correlations without loss.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with directional couplers and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Directional coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementation must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout fidelity; dispersive measurements offer a non-destructive alternative with potential for quantum-limited sensitivity.
method: The authors theoretically model a cavity-based dispersive readout of a spin ensemble, deriving the measurement signal-to-noise ratio and accounting for quantum noise sources such as spin projection noise and photon shot noise.
result: They show that with optimized parameters, the dispersive measurement can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, enabling detection of quantum noise in the ensemble.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-fidelity, quantum-limited readout of solid-state spin ensembles, with applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, revealing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: In quantum thermodynamics, rapid work extraction protocols are often desired, but the fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency in finite-time closed dynamics was not well understood.
method: The authors analyze optimal work extraction from closed quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary evolution, using concepts from quantum speed limits and thermodynamic uncertainty relations.
result: They establish a bound relating the extracted work, the operation time, and the energy fluctuations of the initial state, showing that faster protocols incur a penalty in extractable work.
conclusion: The results provide a fundamental limit on work extraction in finite-time quantum processes, guiding the design of efficient quantum engines and batteries.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the coherent coupling via optical spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, indicating that the spin-cavity system is in the strong coupling regime, which is a key milestone for quantum networking.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond as a promising platform for scalable quantum network nodes, enabling deterministic entanglement generation.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and superradiance/subradiance to create steady-state entanglement.
result: They achieve reconfigurable multipartite entangled states that are robust against inhomogeneous broadening and can be tuned for applications in quantum sensing and topological matter.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with entropy accumulation theorem-based security analysis to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 100 km with composable security, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment by providing both high rates and rigorous security guarantees.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing; monitoring can potentially protect information.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information as a function of system size and measurement rate.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime can scale exponentially with system size in certain regimes, providing a strategy for preserving fragile quantum data.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to dramatically extend quantum information lifetime, offering a practical approach to improve near-term quantum computers.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit their performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of these instabilities is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on single erbium ions coupled to a silicon nanophotonic cavity, measuring spectral jumps and linewidths under various conditions to identify noise sources.
result: They identify charge fluctuations and local electric field noise as dominant causes of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce sensitivity to certain noise sources.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon show promise for quantum networking, but further mitigation of charge noise is needed to achieve transform-limited linewidths.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity, making it challenging to scale entanglement. A control framework that works with inhomogeneous ensembles is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving fields and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging the inhomogeneity as a resource.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead, showing that inhomogeneous ensembles can be programmed to produce useful quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable quantum networks using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, focusing on stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics, using random circuit models.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurement and error correction.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes exhibit improved decodability, which has implications for fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum error correction protocols.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent randomness expansion protocol based on Bell inequality violation, incorporating entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and real-time randomness extraction on-chip.
result: The chip achieves a randomness generation rate of 1.2 Mbps with a certified min-entropy of 0.99 bits per bit, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, high-speed self-testing QRNGs.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion onto a photonic chip, bridging the gap between theoretical security and real-world deployment.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and sensitivity to losses. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical codes.
method: They introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly reduce the number of required emitters and improve loss tolerance compared to symmetric tree-codes.
conclusion: These advances enhance the near-term feasibility of quantum repeaters, bringing practical quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a framework is needed to account for these in a composable manner.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization data into the entropy accumulation theorem (EAT) framework, yielding composable security bounds that depend on the characterized parameters.
result: The method produces rigorous security proofs that can incorporate experimental characterizations, enabling certification of QKD devices with realistic imperfections.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device certification, offering a path toward standardized security evaluation of QKD systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can improve error correction efficiency.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby identifying erasure events.
result: The conversion of relaxation errors into erasures significantly boosts effective coherence times, demonstrating a practical error mitigation strategy.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising platform for fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling erasure conversion, which simplifies error correction.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the feasibility of large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan distances.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (finite-size, composable, and against collective attacks), and experimental implementations (including chip-based and satellite demonstrations).
result: CV quantum communication has reached a mature stage with commercial prototypes, record key rates, and integration into quantum networks; open challenges include long-distance operation and full device independence.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and rapidly advancing technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing research addressing security, distance, and integration.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across scales, challenging conventional methods and providing new insights.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling limit, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors combine Keldysh and Lindblad formalisms to introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines, representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations in open quantum systems.
result: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute correlation functions and response properties for driven dissipative systems, capturing both Markovian and non-Markovian effects.
conclusion: This work offers a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information science.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: Black hole thermodynamics traditionally applies to stationary black holes; this work aims to generalize it to dynamical, non-equilibrium scenarios.
method: Uses the framework of dynamical horizons and derives a first law that holds for black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium.
result: Establishes a first law of black hole mechanics for dynamical horizons, formally extending thermodynamic concepts to non-stationary black holes.
conclusion: The thermodynamic description of black holes is valid even far from equilibrium, deepening the connection between gravity and thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially enhance reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are essential for quantum information processing, but existing methods face limitations in isolation and bandwidth. The authors aim to develop a more effective mechanism for enhancing nonreciprocity.
method: They establish a theoretical framework where squeezing is applied to one cavity to break the symmetry between two coupled cavities, leading to exponentially amplified nonreciprocity in the reservoir-mediated interaction.
result: The proposed mechanism yields an exponential enhancement of nonreciprocity compared to simple coupling scaling, as demonstrated through analytical and numerical calculations.
conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking offers a powerful and generalizable strategy for engineering nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index that characterizes measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, providing a rigorous mechanism for the transition.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism due to noncommutativity of multisite projectors was not well understood.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index based on the algebra of measurement operators and use it to classify phases in a family of measurement-only circuits.
result: The noncommutative index sharply distinguishes volume-law and area-law entangled phases, and its value is analytically computed for several models.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a universal tool for understanding entanglement transitions in measurement-only dynamics, linking to quantum information concepts.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior; the authors aim to characterize subsystem decoherence in a state-independent manner.
method: They investigate the purity of the Choi matrix of the quantum channel describing the reduced dynamics of a subsystem, analyzing its behavior in chaotic systems.
result: The purity of the Choi matrix provides a state-independent measure of decoherence and irreversibility, showing distinct signatures of chaos.
conclusion: This approach offers a robust probe of quantum chaos and decoherence, relevant to understanding the thermodynamic arrow of time in quantum systems.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a practical advantage.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit implementing the higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on small systems and shows potential for scaling to larger systems, providing an estimate of geometric entanglement.
conclusion: The quantum implementation offers a viable approach to estimate geometric entanglement, which is relevant for quantum information theory and quantum computing.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical learning on randomized measurement data to verify approximate k-designs, providing a practical certification method for random quantum states.
motivation: Random quantum states (k-designs) are crucial for many quantum information tasks, but verifying them is challenging. Existing methods are inefficient or require many copies.
method: The authors propose a protocol based on classical shadow tomography and statistical hypothesis testing to certify approximate k-designs using randomized measurements, without needing full state tomography.
result: They demonstrate that their method can efficiently verify k-designs with a polynomial number of measurements, and validate it on numerical simulations and experimental data.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and practical tool for certifying randomness in quantum systems, which is important for benchmarking and quantum advantage experiments.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing surface code stabilizer measurements for Rydberg atoms by suppressing leakage errors improves logical error rates.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions is a promising platform, but leakage errors degrade surface code performance. This work aims to design laser pulses that minimize logical errors rather than just physical gate fidelity.
method: The authors model Rydberg atom dynamics including leakage to non-computational states, identify novel leakage propagation mechanisms, and propose optimized laser-pulse protocols to suppress these errors in surface code stabilizer measurements.
result: The optimized protocols significantly reduce logical error rates in the surface code, outperforming standard gate optimization that targets physical fidelity.
conclusion: Tailoring quantum gates for logical error suppression is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms, and the proposed methods pave the way for efficient error correction in Rydberg platforms.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and resolution of NMR at the nanoscale using NV centers, enabling detection of multiple spin clusters in diamond.
method: The authors use NV centers to polarize nuclear spins, then perform optical readout with stabilized lasers and balanced detection under a highly uniform magnetic field.
result: They resolve sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters, demonstrating high sensitivity and spectral resolution.
conclusion: The technique advances nanoscale NMR and spin sensing, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a new secret-communication protocol based on paraparticle statistics, highlighting their potential for quantum information tasks.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum simulator, addressing the challenge of verifying such advantage in near-term devices.
method: Uses a programmable ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, measuring entanglement entropy and other observables to benchmark against classical simulations.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable, meaning the task is beyond the reach of classical supercomputers, with clear evidence from entanglement growth and system size scaling.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform is a viable candidate for demonstrating practical quantum advantage, and the methods for verification can be extended to other quantum simulators.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic code (e.g., cat code) to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, demonstrating that passive correction can outperform the physical qubit.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for protecting quantum information against photon loss, with potential for simpler experimental realization.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using radiation sources and measuring error correlations.
result: They discover that ionizing radiation causes spatially and temporally correlated phase errors, which persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts pose a fundamental challenge to quantum error correction, requiring new mitigation strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop a theoretical framework linking it to state compression and measurement complexity.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a well-defined monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the resources needed for preparing, compressing, and measuring non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful new tool for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and practical quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the use of critical exponents, finite-size scaling, and dynamical responses near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance estimation precision, providing a systematic approach to design sensors that operate at the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a robust and practical route to achieve high-precision measurements, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout properties, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO may offer new opportunities for spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using experimental measurements and first-principles calculations, demonstrating a 4-ms spin coherence time and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, leading to long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, making it competitive with NV centers in diamond.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to systematically construct better variational ansätze for counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum control tasks compared to standard variational approaches.
conclusion: This provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends learning tasks to quantum states.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier analysis and stabilizer formalism.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other symmetries of unknown quantum states, unifying several symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and quantum state tomography.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and demonstrates cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, addressing a key scalability challenge.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms, hindering scalability. The authors aim to overcome this by multiplexing cavity modes.
method: The authors use a single optical cavity with multiple transverse modes, each addressing a different atom in the array, and demonstrate parallel cavity-enhanced operations such as state readout and entanglement generation.
result: They experimentally show that cavity-mode multiplexing allows simultaneous high-fidelity operations on multiple atoms, significantly increasing the processing speed and scalability of neutral-atom quantum processors.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom arrays, bringing fast quantum operations to large-scale systems.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptography protocols beyond key distribution, addressing both theoretical capabilities and experimental limitations.
method: The paper surveys various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum authentication, quantum oblivious transfer) and discusses their security definitions, proofs, and photonic implementations.
result: It categorizes the main quantum crypto primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and reviews current photonic experimental demonstrations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges; the field is progressing toward more complex protocols.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter leads to inconsistencies; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing the constraints such experiments would place on any future theory of gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified and analyzed, showing that they could test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring a full theory of quantum gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with near-term tabletop experiments potentially providing decisive evidence.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that one-axis twisting dynamics, which typically require all-to-all couplings, can be realized in short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains to generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and spin squeezing.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) is a powerful method for generating quantum resources but requires all-to-all interactions, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by using short-range interactions.
method: The authors propose and analyze a protocol using short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains with engineered interactions to emulate OAT dynamics. They use analytical and numerical methods to study the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing.
result: They demonstrate that scalable quantum resources can be generated with short-range interactions, achieving comparable performance to all-to-all OAT for sufficiently large systems. The protocol is robust to imperfections and finite-range couplings.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a practical platform for generating many-body entanglement and spin squeezing, making OAT-like dynamics accessible in current quantum simulators.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; this work fills that gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: Assumes a qubit is part of a larger composite system and uses the tensor-product structure to derive the form of probability measures.
result: Shows that the only possible probability measures on a qubit are given by density matrices and Born's rule, thus extending Gleason's theorem.
conclusion: The composite system axiom is sufficient to recover the quantum formalism for qubits, providing a foundational justification.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted state preparation and measurement devices.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement (SPAM) device to characterize and then purify noisy SPAM operations via iterative filtering and post-selection.
result: The protocol can suppress preparation and measurement errors to arbitrarily low levels given sufficient resources, and is experimentally feasible with current technology.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to improve qubit SPAM fidelity, which is crucial for near-term quantum devices and quantum network repeaters.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory of full counting statistics after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to provide a universal framework for statistics of conserved quantities after quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of charge transport in integrable systems, treating the quench as a source of initial inhomogeneities.
result: They derive exact formulas for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations follow a large deviation principle with a rate function given by the thermodynamic entropy production.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic description of fluctuations in non-equilibrium quantum systems, bridging quantum quenches and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function computations, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a statistical mechanics model and studying its phase transitions.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength, with the transition point determined by the code's spectral properties.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with critical exceptional points governing their emergence.
motivation: Continuous time-translation symmetry breaking in open quantum systems is a key phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, but the conditions for its appearance are not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze a Lindblad master equation and map the time crystal phase to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, identifying exceptional points as critical boundaries.
result: They demonstrate that the time crystal phase corresponds to a PT-symmetric state and that the transition occurs at exceptional points, providing a clear criterion for emergence.
conclusion: This work bridges time crystals and PT symmetry, offering a new perspective on non-equilibrium phases in open quantum systems relevant to quantum thermodynamics.

title: Satellite-based Quantum Steering With Continuous Variables
authors: Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, And Jieci Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, and Jieci Wang

The Gaussian quantum steering in free space is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication. In this work, we model the free space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating key loss mechanisms including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, turb…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062462] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
