tldr: This paper models free-space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel and analyzes Gaussian quantum steering for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Gaussian quantum steering is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication, but free-space channels introduce loss and noise that degrade steering. The authors aim to model these effects to assess feasibility.
method: They model the free-space channel including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence, and analyze the Gaussian steering of two-mode squeezed states after transmission.
result: They quantify how steering degrades with distance and atmospheric conditions, and identify regimes where steering is preserved.
conclusion: Satellite-based continuous-variable quantum steering is feasible under certain conditions, providing a foundation for future quantum network protocols using satellites.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles, linking disorder statistics to glassy dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how disorder influences relaxation in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the mean and variance of the disorder distribution, validated by exact numerical simulations of interacting quantum spins in tweezer arrays.
result: They show that the relaxation dynamics can be tuned by controlling the disorder statistics, revealing universal scaling behavior.
conclusion: The framework provides a predictive tool for engineering glassy dynamics in programmable quantum simulators, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information storage.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high efficiency.
motivation: Standard EIT memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting speed. Faster storage violates adiabaticity, causing losses.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving (shortcuts to adiabaticity) to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic transitions.
result: The accelerated protocol achieves near-unity storage efficiency and retrieval fidelity in a fraction of the adiabatic time.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-fidelity quantum memory in Rydberg systems, benefiting quantum networks.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: Understanding the formation of discrete time crystals in open systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.
method: The authors study the dynamics of an open system undergoing a phase transition to a discrete time crystal, analyzing defect density and transition delay as functions of quench time.
result: They observe characteristic power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universality in the formation process.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to dissipative discrete time crystal formation, providing insights into non-equilibrium phase transitions in open quantum systems.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems using generalized spin-wave approximations.
motivation: To efficiently simulate open quantum spin systems beyond the reach of exact methods, particularly in regimes where standard approximations fail.
method: Generalizes spin-wave theory to quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, enabling semiclassical treatment of driven-dissipative dynamics.
result: The method accurately captures steady-state properties and dynamics in test cases, showing good agreement with exact solutions where available.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a scalable tool for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in spin systems, relevant to quantum thermal machines and open system dynamics.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper connects the bias in approximate maximum-likelihood estimation for energy-based models to thermodynamic excess work, and investigates minimal-dissipation training.
motivation: Energy-based models (EBMs) are powerful but suffer from biased gradient estimates; understanding this bias from a thermodynamic perspective could lead to more efficient training algorithms.
method: The authors show that the bias of persistent chain EBM training equals the excess work of an overdamped Langevin system, then derive conditions for minimal-dissipation learning using optimal transport and thermodynamic geometry.
result: They find that minimal-dissipation learning is possible when the model distribution is Gaussian, and provide bounds on dissipation for general cases.
conclusion: The work bridges machine learning and thermodynamics, offering a principled way to reduce dissipation in EBM training, though practical applicability may be limited to specific cases.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum self-oscillatory phases and topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamical signatures of classical bifurcations and global phase-space rearrangements in open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the quantum dynamics of driven-dissipative systems exhibiting limit cycles, using phase-space methods and topological flow analysis.
result: They identify quantum signatures of topological flow transitions, such as changes in Wigner function topology and quantum fluctuations near bifurcations.
conclusion: Quantum effects modify classical flow transitions, leading to novel quantum dynamical phases that could be observed in circuit QED or optomechanical setups.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The demonstrated techniques enable new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a transmon qubit with a cosφ coupling element and perform numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the readout process.
result: They demonstrate that the nonlinear coupling suppresses unwanted state transitions during measurement, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout scheme is a promising approach for improving qubit measurement fidelity in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic simulators offer a scalable and configurable platform.
method: The authors decompose a broad class of quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) and implement them on a photonic chip.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity simulation of various quantum field phenomena, including particle creation and entanglement dynamics.
conclusion: The configurable photonic simulator provides an efficient and versatile tool for studying quantum field theories, with potential applications in quantum simulation and fundamental physics.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped ions offer a promising platform. Spin-dependent squeezing can enhance sensitivity beyond standard limits.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, leveraging the coupling between internal spin states and motional degrees of freedom.
result: They show that the proposed scheme achieves the Heisenberg limit for displacement sensing, outperforming classical and standard quantum limits.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces and model selection.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The framework successfully identifies the number and properties of spin bath constituents from simulated and experimental data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and minimal disturbance remains challenging. Existing methods often cause atom loss or heating.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atom arrays. They use a probe-pump scheme in a finite magnetic field to enhance imaging contrast and reduce scattering-induced loss.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging with low atom loss and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, enabling scalable operation.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provides a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation, with potential for integration with other quantum systems.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome performance limits in large-scale quantum processors, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely using superconducting circuit technology and impedance matching techniques.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to traditional designs, breaking through previous performance limits.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for quantum signal amplification and transduction in large-scale quantum processors, facilitating multi-signal processing.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause back-action that destroys quantum information; improving the nondemolition character is crucial for high-fidelity qudit readout.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize disturbance, applied to a silicon quantum dot qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and lower measurement-induced errors compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements across various quantum platforms, benefiting quantum computing and metrology.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive classification that guides future experiments and theory on nonequilibrium stationary states.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but single-photon-level fluorescence signals are noisy and difficult to interpret.
method: The authors combine a neural network trained on simulated and experimental data with Bayesian inference to classify qubit states from weak fluorescence signals.
result: The method achieves readout fidelity above 99% with only a few photons, significantly reducing atom loss and heating compared to conventional thresholding.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical, resource-efficient readout technique for large-scale neutral atom quantum computing.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for nonequilibrium currents in stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: Understanding necessary conditions for directed currents in nonequilibrium systems is fundamental; the ratchet principle is widely used but may be insufficient when hidden conservation laws exist.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying how hidden conservation laws (e.g., due to symmetries or constraints) suppress directed currents despite symmetry breaking.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are violated, refining the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of nonequilibrium transport and highlights the role of conservation laws in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of non-Markovian Decoherent Histories In An Integrable Environment: A Tape-recorder Model For Local Quantum Observables
authors: Nataliya Arefyeva And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Nataliya Arefyeva and Evgeny Polyakov

We propose an alternative approach to the coarse-grained description of quantum evolution that provides an explicit recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories in a controlled way, applicable to non-Markovian and integrable systems. Specifically, we study the local interaction qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062225] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a coarse-grained decoherent histories approach for non-Markovian integrable systems, applied to a tape-recorder model for local observables.
motivation: To develop a controlled method for constructing multitime decoherent histories in non-Markovian and integrable environments, which is relevant for understanding decoherence and emergence of classicality.
method: Introduces a coarse-graining scheme based on local observables and uses the integrability of the environment to construct decoherent histories explicitly.
result: Demonstrates that non-Markovian effects can be captured within the decoherent histories framework, and the tape-recorder model yields consistent histories for local observables.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to study decoherence and the quantum-to-classical transition in complex quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and open systems.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of single-photon routing using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating tunable routing via interatomic interactions.
motivation: To design a tunable quantum photonic router that can control the direction of single photons, which is essential for quantum networks.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems as an effective giant atom coupled to two waveguides, analyzing the system in the strong coupling and weak interaction regime using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The device functions as a tunable router where the output port can be selected by adjusting the interatomic interaction strength or detuning.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-like array provides a feasible platform for quantum photonic routing with tunability, relevant for quantum network applications.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and can be used to certify entanglement.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each coupled to its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and compute the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using the quantum discord and entanglement.
result: They find that the QMA-EUR is affected by the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, and that the lower bound can be tighter than previous bounds.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamics of quantum correlations and uncertainty relations in solid-state systems, which may be relevant for quantum memory and metrology applications.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm to reduce the memory dimension of hidden Markov models using quantum singular value transformation and amplitude amplification.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often require large memory dimensions, making them computationally expensive. The authors aim to leverage quantum computing to compress these models efficiently.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that applies quantum singular value transformation to the transition matrix of an HMM, followed by amplitude amplification to extract a reduced-dimensional representation.
result: The algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup in the dimension reduction process compared to classical methods, and the reduced model maintains high fidelity with the original.
conclusion: Quantum algorithms can effectively reduce the memory dimension of HMMs, offering potential advantages in time-series analysis and machine learning applications.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a new SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a scale that captures operator-ordering sensitivity beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) symmetry and operator ordering, and analyzes its properties for various spin states.
result: The measure quantifies off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases and reveals sensitivity to operator ordering beyond standard coherence measures.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale provides a new tool for characterizing coherence in spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of fundamental triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables in a photonic system.
motivation: While bipartite uncertainty relations are well-studied, tight and experimentally accessible uncertainty relations for three or more observables remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors derive tight triple uncertainty relations based on sum of variances and experimentally test them using a photonic setup with polarization and path degrees of freedom.
result: They observe that the triple uncertainty relations are tighter than any pairwise relation and confirm the theoretical bounds experimentally.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental demonstration of fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum uncertainty in multi-observable scenarios.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin states of a double quantum dot, enabling high-fidelity readout for spin qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing with spin qubits requires fast and high-fidelity readout; Pauli spin blockade readout is promising but limited to distinguishing two states. The authors aim to extend PSB readout to discriminate all four spin states of a pair of spin qubits.
method: They model a double quantum dot coupled to a resonant circuit and simulate the reflected signal phase as a function of gate voltages, using a master equation approach to account for tunneling and relaxation.
result: The four spin states produce distinct phase shifts in the reflected signal, allowing discrimination with fidelity exceeding 99% under realistic parameters.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry can be used for four-state discrimination of spin qubits, providing a practical readout scheme for scaled-up semiconductor quantum processors.

title: Distinction Between The Quantum Two-level System Relaxation Time ${t}_{1}$ And The Effective Lifetime In Single-shot Readouts
authors: Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, And Bhaskaran Muralidharan
abstract:
Author(s): Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, and Bhaskaran Muralidharan

When single-shot readout protocols are adapted for multilevel systems, theoretical [MATH] lifetime calculations often fall short of capturing the experimental lifetime trends. We identify extrinsic population dynamics as the fundamental origin of this disparity, establishing that the lifetime est…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245431] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper distinguishes between the intrinsic relaxation time T1 and the effective lifetime in single-shot readouts of quantum two-level systems, attributing the discrepancy to extrinsic population dynamics.
motivation: Single-shot readout protocols for multilevel systems often yield lifetime estimates that do not match theoretical T1 calculations, hindering accurate characterization of qubit coherence.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating extrinsic population dynamics and validate it against experimental data from quantum dot or similar qubit platforms.
result: They show that the effective lifetime extracted from single-shot readouts can significantly differ from T1 due to state-dependent tunneling and other extrinsic processes.
conclusion: Accurate qubit characterization requires careful modeling of readout dynamics to extract the intrinsic T1, which is crucial for improving qubit coherence and gate fidelity.

title: Coupling-energy Driven Pumping Through Quantum Dots: Role Of Coherences
authors: Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, And Nikodem Szpak
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, and Nikodem Szpak

We study the impact of off-resonant tunneling and coherences on the electron pumping through quantum dots. Thereby, we focus on two electron-pump setups where lowest-order tunneling processes are suppressed and the pump is exclusively driven by modulations of the coupling energy. The first setup is …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235152] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron pumping through quantum dots driven solely by coupling energy modulations, focusing on the role of off-resonant tunneling and coherences.
motivation: Understanding how coherences affect pumping in quantum dots is important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum transport.
method: The authors analyze two pump setups where lowest-order tunneling is suppressed, using theoretical models to study the impact of coherences and off-resonant tunneling.
result: They find that coherences can significantly influence the pumped current, and off-resonant tunneling provides additional pathways.
conclusion: Coherences play a crucial role in coupling-energy-driven pumping, and their control could enhance quantum dot-based devices.

title: Entanglement Rényi Negativity Across The Finite-temperature Transition In The $o(3)$ Universality Class
authors: Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, and Zheng Yan

The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions remains an open question, particularly for continuous symmetry breaking where zero-temperature Goldstone modes generate long-range correlations. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the third Rényi …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245145] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the third Rényi negativity across a finite-temperature phase transition in the O(3) universality class using quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions, especially with continuous symmetry breaking, is not well understood.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the third Rényi negativity across the transition.
result: The behavior of the Rényi negativity across the finite-temperature transition is characterized.
conclusion: The study provides insights into entanglement at finite temperature in systems with continuous symmetry breaking.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are not fully violated, due to active fluctuations.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter and systems with non-thermal fluctuations is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and both passive (thermal) and active (non-thermal) noise sources, using theoretical models and simulations to study current generation.
result: They find that active fluctuations can induce directed currents even when all symmetries are nominally violated, challenging the traditional interpretation of the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the role of activity in non-equilibrium transport, with implications for designing nanoscale motors and understanding biological processes.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can stay near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and biological systems.
method: The authors model a swimmer with active control and passive drift, using stochastic thermodynamics to derive optimal strategies.
result: They find a trade-off between localization accuracy and the thermodynamic cost of swimming, with optimal strategies combining passive and active phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the fundamental limits of navigation in fluctuating environments, linking control, information, and thermodynamics.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the area enclosed by the atomic array.
motivation: Rotation sensing is important for navigation and fundamental physics; atom-cavity systems offer a platform for high-precision measurements.
method: The system operates near a critical transition, and cavity-emitted light is used to probe changes in rotation frequency.
result: The sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, indicating potential for high-performance rotation sensing.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system is a promising candidate for rotation sensing, leveraging quantum optical techniques.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To demonstrate quantum synchronization in a controlled platform, bridging quantum thermodynamics and quantum information.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators.
result: Synchronized state observed via a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.
conclusion: Trapped ions provide a viable platform for studying quantum synchronization, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum networks.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical systems, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics scenarios.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a practical and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential impact on quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, demonstrating insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by noise, especially common-mode noise in differential measurements. The authors aim to develop a scalable and robust approach for quantum sensor networks.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation using quantum metrology techniques.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being immune to common-mode phase fluctuations, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks that can operate in realistic noisy conditions, advancing quantum metrology.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered dissipation to prepare superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully realize superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states, with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and fluctuation theorems in the continuum limit.
result: Unifies previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables in both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics in systems with discrete state transitions.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, characterizing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing qubit errors in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to map out excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance conditions leading to ionization.
result: They observe clear signatures of Landau-Zener transitions and quantify the ionization rates under various drive parameters.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms and suggest strategies to mitigate ionization for better qubit performance.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing time and thermalization time in quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite for many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and have implications for digital quantum simulation and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulses to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints and imperfections.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method, extracting noise cross-correlations and bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise spectroscopy in quantum devices, aiding in the understanding and mitigation of decoherence.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve robust photon blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics as a function of ensemble size.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires efficient error correction and hardware-specific optimizations to reduce space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture demonstrates a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Fourier neural operators are trained on time-series data to learn the mapping from initial states to future observables, leveraging spectral methods for efficiency.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond training data and learns effective Floquet Hamiltonians, demonstrating generalization.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a powerful tool for simulating and understanding periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. This work aims to design device-tailored sequences that are scalable.
method: The authors map the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of sequences that cancel k-local noise.
result: They demonstrate that the sequence length depends only on the locality k of the noise, not on the total number of qubits, and provide explicit constructions for various noise models.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical, scalable noise mitigation for quantum devices.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to the circuit's expressivity and noise level.
result: They show that noise can help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, and provide quantitative estimates of loss function concentration.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by balancing noise and expressivity, guiding the design of trainable variational quantum algorithms.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional mechanical degrees of freedom is challenging.
method: The authors engineer tailored optical interactions in a fully optical system to create an effective negative-mass oscillator that coherently cancels quantum backaction noise.
result: They demonstrate successful cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum sensing.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized time evolution, where the Hamiltonian simulation step uses randomized product formulas that trade some accuracy for drastically reduced circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard deterministic product formulas.
conclusion: Partially randomized phase estimation is a practical technique to make near-term quantum phase estimation more feasible, especially for quantum chemistry applications.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, and validate it using a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used as a proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, enabling better error mitigation and algorithm performance prediction.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates leakage-protected idle operation of a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors degrade qubit performance; protecting idle operation without active feedback is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons in a triangular quantum dot to be equal, opening a gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, demonstrating improved qubit coherence.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple, passive method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a comprehensive overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper presents a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, comparing various simulation techniques such as hierarchical equations of motion, quantum master equations, and stochastic methods.
result: It highlights commonalities and differences among methods, offering guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework aids in understanding and selecting simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems, benefiting research in quantum thermodynamics and information.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium surveys the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and realizing quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and resource reduction.
motivation: Qudits offer potential advantages over qubits in certain quantum computing tasks, such as reducing the number of operations or physical resources needed for implementing multiqubit gates.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions using qudits (e.g., Toffoli gate with qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can simplify gate decompositions, reduce circuit depth, and improve fidelity in some cases, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for near-term devices, though challenges remain in qudit control and error correction.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is a key challenge for solid-state spin qubits.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, discussing how atomistic and electronic structure affect decoherence.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of spin qubits with long coherence times.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian environments affect quantum steering ellipsoids, a geometric representation of bipartite quantum correlations.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric tool to visualize steerability, but realistic open-system dynamics can degrade them; understanding protection mechanisms is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors model two qubits coupled to independent non-Markovian reservoirs and analyze the evolution of the steering ellipsoid volume and shape using exact master equations.
result: Non-Markovian memory effects can partially protect the steering ellipsoid from collapse, preserving steerability longer than Markovian environments.
conclusion: Engineering non-Markovian environments may help preserve quantum steering in practical quantum communication and cryptography protocols.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of different state preparation protocols for topological states, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Numerical study of two particle number-conserving protocols: thermal coupling to a cold bath and engineered dissipation.
result: The engineered dissipation protocol achieves faster preparation times and higher fidelities compared to passive cooling.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state engineering.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum expectation landscapes is often intractable, but for small subregions, efficient surrogates may be possible, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors propose a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using techniques from classical shadow tomography or machine learning.
