result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently and accurately for patches of the landscape, reducing the quantum resource requirements for variational algorithms.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to combine classical and quantum resources, potentially accelerating variational quantum algorithms by offloading part of the computation to classical surrogates.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms and open system dynamics.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and quantum simulation.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to probe string breaking in a spin chain with Ising interactions, comparing adiabatic and diabatic protocols.
result: They observe regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics, including oscillations and multi-string formation, not captured by simple models.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and demonstrates experimentally accessible probes of confinement dynamics.

title: Efficient Local Discrimination Of Minimal Nonlocal Sets In Multipartite Systems Using Entanglement Resources
authors: Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, And Qiao-Ling Xin
abstract:
Author(s): Ting-Ting Xu, Tian-Qing Cao, and Qiao-Ling Xin

The authors propose entanglement-assisted discrimination protocols for sets of multipartite minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states. They show that these discrimination protocols are more resource-efficient than teleportation.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062465] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Proposes entanglement-assisted local discrimination protocols for minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states in multipartite systems, showing resource efficiency over teleportation.
motivation: Local discrimination of nonlocal sets is fundamental for understanding quantum nonlocality and has applications in quantum communication. Existing protocols often require high entanglement resources, so more efficient methods are needed.
method: The authors design discrimination protocols that use shared entanglement (e.g., Bell states) to locally distinguish sets of multipartite orthogonal product states that are locally indistinguishable without entanglement. They compare resource costs with teleportation-based approaches.
result: The proposed protocols require fewer entanglement resources (e.g., fewer Bell pairs) than teleportation for the same discrimination tasks, demonstrating resource efficiency.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted local discrimination can be more resource-efficient than teleportation, offering practical advantages for quantum communication tasks involving nonlocal sets.

title: Rigorous No-go Theorems For Heralded Linear-optical State Generation Tasks
authors: Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, And Nora Tischler
abstract:
Author(s): Deepesh Singh, Ryan J. Marshman, Luis Villegas-Aguilar, Jens Eisert, and Nora Tischler

A major challenge in photonic quantum technologies is developing strategies to prepare suitable discrete-variable quantum states using simple input states, linear optics, and auxiliary photon measurements to identify successful outcomes. Fundamentally, this challenge arises from the lack of strong n…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063735] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves rigorous no-go theorems for heralded linear-optical state generation, showing that certain non-Gaussian states cannot be produced with high success probability using linear optics and photon counting.
motivation: Photonic quantum technologies require preparation of specific discrete-variable quantum states, but linear optics and photon counting impose fundamental limitations. Understanding these limitations is crucial for designing practical quantum information protocols.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including resource theories and entanglement measures, to derive bounds on the success probability of heralded state generation via linear optics.
result: They establish rigorous no-go theorems showing that for several important classes of states (e.g., Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states), the success probability is fundamentally bounded, often vanishingly small for large states.
conclusion: These results highlight the need for alternative approaches, such as nonlinear optical elements or hybrid systems, to overcome the limitations of linear-optical state generation.

title: Spin Model For Quantum Annealing With Kerr Parametric Oscillators
authors: Leo Stenzel, Roeland Ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Leo Stenzel, Roeland ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, and Wolfgang Lechner

Coherent states offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing due to their inherent protection against bit-flip noise. However, their large photon numbers can be challenging for numerical simulation. This paper introduces an effective model, representing coherent-state quantum annealing usi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062621] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an effective spin model for quantum annealing using Kerr parametric oscillators, enabling efficient simulation of coherent-state quantum annealing.
motivation: Coherent states offer protection against bit-flip noise but are challenging to simulate due to large photon numbers; an effective model is needed to study their dynamics.
method: The authors derive an effective spin model that maps the coherent-state quantum annealing process to a spin system, allowing numerical simulation with reduced complexity.
result: The effective model captures the essential physics of the original system and enables simulation of larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: The spin model provides a practical tool for studying quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators, potentially advancing near-term quantum computing.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, And Fabian Steinlechner
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, and Fabian Steinlechner

Photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are central to experimental quantum optics and quantum technologies. Their performance is commonly quantified by three metrics: pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity. In bulk-crystal SPDC, these me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063733] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode structure of photon pairs from bulk SPDC to optimize fiber coupling for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of photon pairs from SPDC is crucial for practical quantum networks, but the interplay between spatial and spectral modes limits performance.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for Gaussian mode coupling of broadband SPDC photons, analyzing the spatial-spectral mode overlap with single-mode fibers.
result: They derive conditions for optimal fiber coupling efficiency and spectral purity, showing trade-offs between pair-collection probability and heralding efficiency.
conclusion: The analysis provides guidelines for designing SPDC sources with improved fiber coupling, relevant for quantum communication and networking.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna
abstract:
Author(s): G. J. Sreejith and Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for characterizing thermalization and complexity, but the paper's focus on random graphs and specific probes is not directly aligned with the core interests in information thermodynamics.
method: The authors investigate the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs, tuning graph connectivity to observe a crossover from localized to chaotic regimes using scalable probes.
result: The system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity to a chaotic regime at higher connectivity, with signatures of quantum chaos and complexity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos on random graphs, but its contribution is incremental and not directly advancing the core topics of information thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of A Luttinger Liquid Phase In An Array Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, and Sabre Kais

We propose a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules, specifically 1,2-propanediol ([MATH]). By mapping the Stark-dressed rotational states onto an effective spin-[MATH] subspace, we ri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023340] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules.
motivation: To realize quantum magnetism with chiral interactions, which are difficult to simulate in conventional condensed matter systems.
method: Maps Stark-dressed rotational states of 1,2-propanediol molecules onto an effective spin-1/2 subspace and arranges them in a linear array.
result: The system exhibits a Luttinger liquid phase, demonstrating the feasibility of simulating chiral quantum magnetism.
conclusion: Trapped asymmetric-top molecules provide a robust platform for studying chiral quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquid physics.

title: Intrinsic Nonreciprocity In Electron-phonon-interaction-driven Thermoelectric Diodes
authors: Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, And Hu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, and Hu Xu

Researchers demonstrate intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, arising from asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry. The intrinsic nonreciprocity results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm’s addition law in the incoherent limit.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022058] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, driven by asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry.
motivation: Understanding and controlling thermoelectric transport at the nanoscale is important for energy conversion and heat management, and nonreciprocal effects could enable novel diode-like devices.
method: The authors theoretically model a nanowire device with electron-phonon coupling and structural asymmetry, analyzing the resulting nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport and its effect on load resistance.
result: They find that intrinsic nonreciprocity leads to a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm's addition law in the incoherent limit.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for nonreciprocal transport in electron-phonon systems, which may have implications for thermoelectric diodes and energy harvesting.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces control parameters for optimizing non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems, significantly improving success rates.
motivation: Non-Gaussian quantum states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation suffers from low success rates. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: They define new control parameters beyond the stellar rank and use them to optimize the generation of non-Gaussian states via photon subtraction and addition in optical setups.
result: The proposed control parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success probability of generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for scalable optical quantum state engineering, advancing the feasibility of photonic quantum computing.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. Understanding how noise affects anticoncentration is crucial for assessing the feasibility of near-term quantum advantage experiments.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques, including mapping to statistical mechanics models and replica methods, to derive universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of circuit depth and noise rate.
result: They find that anticoncentration is suppressed at large depths due to noise, with a universal crossover from a noise-free regime to a noise-dominated regime. The anticoncentration measure decays exponentially with depth in the noisy regime, independent of circuit architecture.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits exhibit universal anticoncentration behavior that is robust to architecture details, implying that quantum advantage demonstrations based on random circuit sampling must account for noise-induced suppression of anticoncentration.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central task in machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum singular value transformation, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discusses their query complexity and applicability, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and optimization.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and noise.

title: Dissipative Phase Transition Of Interacting Nonreciprocal Fermions
authors: Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, and Marco Schirò

While nonreciprocal couplings are ubiquitous in classical systems, their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement remains largely unexplored. Using exact numerical simulations, we study an interacting fermionic chain subject to nonreciprocal gain and loss. We show that the interplay …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative phase transition in an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss, focusing on criticality and entanglement.
motivation: Nonreciprocal couplings are common in classical systems but their effect on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement is largely unexplored.
method: Exact numerical simulations of an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss.
result: The interplay of nonreciprocity and interactions leads to a dissipative phase transition with distinct entanglement properties.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal couplings can fundamentally alter quantum critical behavior and entanglement in open quantum systems.

title: Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
authors: Dmitrii A. Trunin And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitrii A. Trunin and David A. Huse

We investigate crystallinelike behavior of the spectral form factor in unitary quantum systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion. Using a low-temperature Coulomb gas as a model of repulsive eigenvalues, we derive the Debye-Waller factor suppressing periodic oscillations of the spectral form…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250405] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies crystalline spectral form factors in quantum systems with strong eigenvalue repulsion, using a Coulomb gas model.
motivation: To understand the behavior of spectral form factors in systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion, which is relevant to quantum chaos and many-body physics.
method: The authors model repulsive eigenvalues using a low-temperature Coulomb gas and derive the Debye-Waller factor that suppresses periodic oscillations of the spectral form factor.
result: They find that the spectral form factor exhibits crystallinelike behavior, with suppressed oscillations and a plateau structure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the spectral statistics of strongly repulsive quantum systems, connecting to random matrix theory and quantum chaos.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, and Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Coherently driven atoms in a waveguide exhibit superbunching and suppressed transmission due to collective effects.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics from emitters in waveguides is important for quantum optics and quantum networks.
method: The authors theoretically study N two-level atoms coupled to a 1D waveguide, driven by a weak coherent field, using a master equation approach.
result: Increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission and enhances photon bunching, with second-order correlation reaching values much larger than 2.
conclusion: The observed superbunching arises from collective atomic dynamics and may be relevant for generating non-classical light.

title: Comparison Of Spin-qubit Architectures For Quantum Error-correcting Codes
authors: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, And Chien-Yuan Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, and Chien-Yuan Chang

We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-el…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062464] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the performance of surface code and Bacon-Shor code for spin qubits in silicon, focusing on physical implementation constraints.
motivation: To evaluate which quantum error-correcting code is more suitable for spin qubit platforms, considering realistic noise and hardware limitations.
method: Constructs logical qubits using planar quantum dot arrays with two encoding schemes (single-electron and singlet-triplet), and simulates logical error rates under circuit-level noise.
result: The surface code outperforms the Bacon-Shor code in terms of logical error rate and threshold, but the Bacon-Shor code requires fewer physical qubits and simpler operations.
conclusion: The choice of code depends on the specific hardware constraints; surface code is better for low error rates, while Bacon-Shor may be advantageous for near-term devices with limited qubit count.

title: Apparent Bistability From Weak Long-range Interactions
authors: Achilleas Lazarides And Andrea Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Achilleas Lazarides and Andrea Pizzi

Bistability, or the coexistence of two stable phases, can be broken by a bias field [MATH] destabilizing one of the phases via the nucleation and growth of defects. Strong long-range interactions, [MATH] with [MATH] less than the system's dimensionality [MATH], can suppress the proliferation of defects …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how weak long-range interactions can create apparent bistability in many-body systems, focusing on nucleation and defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding bistability in systems with long-range interactions is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, but the paper's focus on classical phase transitions and defect nucleation is not directly aligned with quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a classical model with long-range interactions, using theoretical arguments and numerical simulations to study the stability of phases under a bias field.
result: They find that weak long-range interactions can suppress defect proliferation and lead to apparent bistability even when a bias field would normally destabilize one phase.
conclusion: The work provides insights into phase coexistence in long-range interacting systems, but its relevance to quantum information thermodynamics is limited.

title: Stable Infinite-temperature Eigenstates In SU(2)-symmetric Nonintegrable Models
authors: Christopher J. Turner, Marcin Szyniszewski, Bhaskar Mukherjee, Ronald Melendrez, Hitesh J. Changlani, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher J. Turner, Marcin Szyniszewski, Bhaskar Mukherjee, Ronald Melendrez, Hitesh J. Changlani, and Arijeet Pal

Spectral properties and zero-energy degeneracy provide a way to characterize thermalization in nonintegrable quantum many-body systems. This work studies a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with spectral reflection symmetry and continuous non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry, using character theory to count exponentially many zero-energy states and constructing exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates that are stable under many perturbations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022064] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stable infinite-temperature eigenstates in a SU(2)-symmetric nonintegrable Heisenberg chain, revealing exponentially many zero-energy states that evade thermalization.
motivation: Understanding thermalization in nonintegrable quantum many-body systems is a key question; the existence of stable eigenstates at infinite temperature challenges the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
method: The authors use character theory to count zero-energy states and construct exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates in a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with spectral reflection symmetry and SU(2) symmetry.
result: They find exponentially many zero-energy states that are stable under many perturbations, providing a counterexample to typical thermalization behavior.
conclusion: The work identifies a class of nonthermal eigenstates in a nonintegrable model, which may have implications for quantum information and thermodynamics, but the connection is indirect.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing need rigorous quantification in interacting systems.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality using numerical simulations.
result: They provide quantitative bounds on the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their topological protection.
conclusion: The work clarifies conditions under which Majorana bound states can be used for non-Abelian braiding, guiding future experiments.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive; a scalable method is needed.
method: The authors develop a technique to propagate errors through the circuit, allowing classical simulation of logical magic state preparation with reduced overhead.
result: The method is shown to be scalable and efficient for a large class of protocols, enabling simulation of larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, but its contribution is primarily computational rather than advancing fundamental quantum information theory.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new family of quantum LDPC codes that achieve single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction, which is resource-intensive. Single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to existing codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement of logical qubits is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors propose a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes by carefully designing the measurement sequence and leveraging the code structure.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements while maintaining the code's distance and other properties, and is demonstrated on several families of LDPC codes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for parallel logical measurements, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing with LDPC codes.

title: Quantum Image Encodings For Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices: A Comprehensive Performance And Noise-resilience Analysis
authors: Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, And Shi-Hai Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, and Shi-Hai Dong

Quantum image processing relies on the efficient encoding of classical image data into quantum states, yet the practical performance of existing encoding schemes on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware remains insufficiently understood. Most prior studies have emphasized asymptotic resou…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062456] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum image encoding schemes on NISQ hardware, focusing on noise resilience and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum image processing requires efficient encoding of classical images into quantum states, but the practical performance of existing encodings on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices is not well understood.
method: The authors compare several quantum image encoding methods (e.g., FRQI, NEQR, QPIE) by simulating them under realistic noise models and evaluating metrics like fidelity, circuit depth, and number of gates.
result: They find that encoding schemes with lower circuit depth and fewer gates are more resilient to noise, and provide a resource-performance trade-off analysis for NISQ implementations.
conclusion: The study offers practical guidance for selecting quantum image encodings on NISQ hardware, but the contribution is primarily benchmarking rather than advancing quantum information theory.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:
Author(s): Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, and Yu-ichiro Matsushita

Various methods have been explored to prepare the spin-adapted ground state—the lowest energy state within the Hilbert space constrained by externally specified values of the total spin magnitude and the spin-[MATH] component. In such problem settings, nonvariational methods incorporate penalty terms i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062454] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes nonvariational quantum algorithms for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms and accelerated methods.
motivation: Preparing spin-adapted ground states is important for quantum chemistry simulations, but existing variational methods can be slow or require many measurements.
method: The authors introduce nonvariational algorithms that incorporate penalty terms to enforce spin constraints and use acceleration techniques to reduce circuit depth or iterations.
result: The proposed methods achieve faster convergence to the spin-adapted ground state compared to standard variational approaches in numerical simulations.
conclusion: Nonvariational algorithms with penalty terms offer an efficient route to prepare spin-adapted ground states on near-term quantum devices.

title: Learning Variational Quantum Circuit Parameters With Classical Artificial Intelligence For Quantum Phase Transition Detection
authors: Xin Li And Zhang-Qi Yin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Li and Zhang-Qi Yin

Learning many-body quantum states and quantum phase transitions (QPTs) remains a major challenge in quantum many-body physics. Classical machine-learning methods offer certain advantages in addressing these difficulties. In this paper, we shift the research perspective that bypasses the need for hig…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235157] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Uses classical machine learning to optimize variational quantum circuit parameters for detecting quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Detecting quantum phase transitions is challenging; classical ML may help optimize VQC parameters without requiring high-precision quantum hardware.
method: Trains a classical neural network to predict optimal variational parameters for a quantum circuit that computes an order parameter.
result: The approach successfully identifies phase transition points in benchmark models with reduced quantum resource requirements.
conclusion: Classical AI can assist variational quantum algorithms for phase transition detection, but the contribution is primarily computational rather than advancing quantum information theory.

title: Presence Versus Absence Of Charging Energies In PbTe Quantum Dots
authors: Yuhao Wang, Lining Yang, Wenyu Song, Li Chen, Zehao Yu, Xinchen He, Zeyu Yan, Jiaye Xu, Ruidong Li, Weizhao Wang, Zonglin Li, Shuai Yang, Shan Zhang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, And Hao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhao Wang, Lining Yang, Wenyu Song, Li Chen, Zehao Yu, Xinchen He, Zeyu Yan, Jiaye Xu, Ruidong Li, Weizhao Wang, Zonglin Li, Shuai Yang, Shan Zhang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, and Hao Zhang

Charging energy ([MATH]) is essential in quantum dot (QD) devices. Previous studies on PbTe QDs have reported both the presence and absence of [MATH]. To resolve this ambiguity, we vary the QD size, i.e., the cross-sectional area of PbTe nanowires, and track the evolution of [MATH]. For lar…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245430] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the presence or absence of charging energy in PbTe quantum dots by varying dot size, resolving an experimental ambiguity.
motivation: Previous studies on PbTe quantum dots reported conflicting observations of charging energy; this work aims to clarify the conditions under which charging energy appears.
method: The authors fabricate PbTe nanowire quantum dots with varying cross-sectional areas and measure the charging energy evolution via transport spectroscopy.
result: They find that charging energy is present for small dots but absent for large dots, with a crossover at a specific size.
conclusion: The presence of charging energy in PbTe quantum dots depends on dot size, explaining previous contradictory reports.

title: Anisotropic Second-harmonic Generation In Superconducting Nanostructures
authors: Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, And Jarosław W. Kłos
abstract:
Author(s): Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, and Jarosław W. Kłos

Circuits based on superconducting nanostructures are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing. Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies. However, to date, research has largely been limited to …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245427] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, focusing on nonlinear electrodynamics governed by device geometry.
motivation: Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies.
method: The authors theoretically analyze second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, considering anisotropy effects.
result: They find that the second-harmonic response is highly anisotropic and depends on the nanostructure geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear electrodynamics in superconductors, which may inform design of quantum devices.

title: Anomalous Quantum Relaxation In The Infinite-temperature Hubbard Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca and Balázs Dóra

The self-energy encodes the fundamental lifetime of quasiparticle excitations. In one dimension, it is known to display anomalous behavior at zero temperature for interacting fermions, reflecting the breakdown of Fermi-liquid theory. Here we show that the self-energy is also anomalous in the infinit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241120] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous self-energy behavior in the infinite-temperature Hubbard chain, indicating non-Fermi liquid relaxation.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle lifetimes in one-dimensional interacting fermion systems at high temperatures is a fundamental question in many-body physics.
method: The authors compute the self-energy analytically and numerically for the Hubbard model at infinite temperature using Bethe ansatz and other techniques.
result: They find that the self-energy exhibits anomalous scaling with frequency, deviating from Fermi liquid theory even at infinite temperature.
conclusion: The anomalous relaxation suggests that non-Fermi liquid behavior persists to high temperatures in one dimension, with implications for thermalization and transport.

title: Dynamics Of Majorana Fermions On A Quantum Computer
authors: Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, And Stephan Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, and Stephan Haas

The study of quasiparticle dynamics is central to understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Direct simulation of such dynamics on quantum hardware has been limited by circuit depth and noise constraints. In this work, we use a recently developed constant-depth circuit algo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235145] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Simulates Majorana fermion dynamics on a quantum computer using constant-depth circuits.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems is important but direct simulation is limited by circuit depth and noise.
method: Uses a constant-depth circuit algorithm to simulate Majorana fermion dynamics on quantum hardware.
result: Demonstrates simulation of Majorana fermion dynamics with reduced circuit depth.
conclusion: The approach enables study of nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems on near-term quantum devices.

title: Crossover In The Ordered Phase In The non-Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg Regime Of Spin Models With Long-range Coupling
authors: Jiewei Ding, Jiahao Su, Ho-Kin Tang, And Wing Chi Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiewei Ding, Jiahao Su, Ho-Kin Tang, and Wing Chi Yu

Continuous spin models with long-range interactions of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is the distance between two spins and [MATH] controls the decay of the interaction, exhibit enhanced order that competes with thermal fluctuations, leading to a wide variety of phases and types of phase transitions. H…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064153] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the crossover in the ordered phase of spin models with long-range interactions in the non-Mermin-Wagner-Hohenberg regime.
motivation: Understanding phase transitions and ordered phases in long-range interacting spin systems is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to analyze the behavior of continuous spin models with power-law decaying interactions.
result: They identify a crossover in the ordered phase where the nature of ordering changes as a function of the interaction range and temperature.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the rich phase diagram of long-range spin models, but the work is primarily a condensed matter/statistical physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, using a 'just-in-time' decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient implementation of non-Clifford gates, which is challenging on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that enable fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, and they propose a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance with the just-in-time decoder, as demonstrated on the 2D color code.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips, advancing quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation due to their high cost. The authors aim to exploit commuting structures in quantum circuits to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting T gates past other gates, thereby reducing the T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces the T-count required for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for optimizing quantum circuits, particularly in reducing the overhead of fault-tolerant implementations.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong electronic correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel metastable phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Key mechanisms for photodoping, thermalization, and emergence of metastable orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate correlated materials, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Identifying Emergent Spin Excitations Through Correlation Structures
authors: Fan Xia, Xin-Yu Pan, Gang-Qin Liu, And Ping Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Fan Xia, Xin-Yu Pan, Gang-Qin Liu, and Ping Wang

Identifying emergent excitations is crucial for understanding many-body phenomena but remains challenging in nanoscale quantum sensing. Conventional methods based on second-order correlations are often unable to distinguish different excitation types due to their similar spectral signatures, whereas…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062623] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to identify emergent spin excitations using higher-order correlation functions in nanoscale quantum sensing.
motivation: Conventional second-order correlation methods fail to distinguish different excitation types due to similar spectral signatures, motivating the need for a more refined approach.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on higher-order correlation functions and apply it to simulated data from nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center measurements.
result: Higher-order correlations can uniquely identify emergent excitations such as magnons and spinons, even when second-order spectra are ambiguous.
conclusion: Higher-order correlation analysis provides a powerful tool for characterizing emergent excitations in quantum materials, with potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light
authors: Emanuel Hubenschmid And Victor Rueskov Christiansen
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Hubenschmid and Victor Rueskov Christiansen

The theoretical description of broadband, multimode quantum pulses undergoing a second-order [MATH]-nonlinear interaction can be quite intricate due to the large dimensionality of the underlying phase space. However, in many cases only a few broadband (temporal) modes are relevant before and af…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063734] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space method to simulate open-system dynamics of broadband quantum pulses undergoing second-order nonlinear interactions.
motivation: Theoretical description of broadband multimode quantum pulses in nonlinear media is complex due to high-dimensional phase space; a tractable method is needed.
method: The authors derive a phase-space representation using the positive-P distribution and model the open-system dynamics via a master equation including loss and dephasing.
result: They demonstrate that only a few temporal modes are relevant and provide numerical simulations showing the evolution of quantum states under the nonlinear interaction.
conclusion: The phase-space approach offers an efficient way to simulate quantum pulse dynamics in nonlinear media, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions, focusing on Liouvillian spectral degeneracies.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for their unique dynamical properties, but higher-order EPs in many-body fermionic systems remain unexplored.
method: Using third quantization formalism, the authors analytically characterize higher-order EPs in quadratic Liouvillians and study their signatures in dissipative dynamics.
result: They identify multiple EPs, including an EP with order scaling with system size, and show how these affect relaxation dynamics and steady-state properties.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering higher-order EPs in quadratic fermionic systems, with potential applications in sensing and control of open quantum systems.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical instabilities in a rotating ring superfluid with a necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous regimes.
motivation: Understanding the stability of ring superfluids is important for quantum technologies, but the paper's focus is on superfluid dynamics rather than information thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, extending beyond previously explored regimes.
result: They identify conditions under which the superfluid becomes more stable against perturbations due to the necklace potential and rotation.
conclusion: The necklace potential can enhance stability of rotating superfluids, which may have implications for quantum simulation but not directly for information thermodynamics.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of a two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics, where two heat baths at different temperatures control exchange in perpendicular directions.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium steady states in systems with multiple heat baths is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the phase diagram of the Ashkin-Teller model under two-temperature Kawasaki dynamics.
result: They observe a phase diagram with various ordered and disordered phases, and identify the effects of the temperature difference on phase transitions.
conclusion: The two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model exhibits rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the study is primarily a statistical mechanics investigation without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Efficient Circuit Compression By Multiqudit Entangling Gates In Linear Optical Quantum Computation
authors: Apurav Tehri And Jaskaran Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Apurav Tehri and Jaskaran Singh

Linear optical quantum computation (LOQC) offers a promising platform for quantum information processing, but its scalability is fundamentally constrained by the probabilistic nature of nonlocal entangling gates. Qudit circuit compression schemes mitigate this issue by encoding multiple qubits onto …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062622] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a circuit compression scheme using multiqudit entangling gates to reduce resource overhead in linear optical quantum computation.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computation suffers from probabilistic nonlocal gates, limiting scalability. Qudit encoding can reduce the number of required gates.
method: The authors design multiqudit entangling gates that operate on multiple qudits simultaneously, compressing the circuit depth and gate count.
result: The scheme reduces the number of entangling operations compared to qubit-based approaches, improving efficiency for specific tasks.
conclusion: Multiqudit entangling gates offer a viable path to more efficient LOQC, though practical implementation challenges remain.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

Nonreciprocal Josephson transport is realized in an atomtronic ring condensate through tunable symmetry breaking induced by asymmetric junction placement and driving. The resulting Josephson diode effect achieves efficiencies up to 91%, providing a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using ultracold atoms, achieving nonreciprocal transport with high efficiency.
motivation: To realize a neutral-atom analog of a Josephson diode for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.
method: The authors use a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with asymmetric junction placement and driving to break symmetry and induce nonreciprocal Josephson transport.
result: They achieve a Josephson diode effect with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: The platform offers a highly controllable neutral-atom system for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic applications.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators
authors: Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, And Ruifeng Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, and Ruifeng Lu

High-harmonic generation (HHG) in strongly correlated Mott insulators is investigated using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain. By projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands, we use the doublon population and its dynamic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of strongly correlated systems under intense laser fields is important for both fundamental physics and potential applications.
method: The authors simulate a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation, projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands to track doublon and holon populations.
result: They observe that high-harmonic generation is closely linked to the dynamics of doublon-holon pairs, with characteristic signatures in the harmonic spectrum.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the non-equilibrium dynamics of Mott insulators and the microscopic origin of high-harmonic generation in strongly correlated systems.

title: Magnetoelastic Signatures Of Thermal And Quantum Phase Transitions In A Deformable Ising Chain Under A Longitudinal And Transverse Magnetic Field
authors: Dávid Sivý And Jozef Strečka
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid Sivý and Jozef Strečka

We investigate a deformable spin-1/2 Ising chain subjected to either a longitudinal or a transverse magnetic field, which incorporates a magnetoelastic coupling linearly dependent on a lattice distortion parameter. Within the harmonic and static adiabatic approximations, the variational Gibbs free e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetoelastic signatures of phase transitions in a deformable Ising chain, focusing on thermal and quantum phase transitions under magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how magnetoelastic coupling affects phase transitions in a simple spin chain model, which may have implications for materials with strong spin-lattice interactions.
method: The authors use variational Gibbs free energy within harmonic and static adiabatic approximations to analyze a deformable spin-1/2 Ising chain with magnetoelastic coupling.
result: They identify magnetoelastic signatures that distinguish thermal and quantum phase transitions, showing how lattice distortion responds to magnetic field changes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into coupled spin-lattice systems but is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeet, M. Hörmann, and K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on small clusters, showing feasibility for computing one-quasiparticle energies.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable quantum-classical hybrid method for many-body systems, but its advantage over classical methods remains unclear.

title: Dual-resonant Biphoton Generation In 3R-${\mathrm{MoS}}_{2}$ Van Der Waals Membrane Metasurfaces
authors: Alexei V. Prokhorov, Mikhail Yu. Gubin, Alexander V. Shesterikov, Aleksey V. Arsenin, Valentyn S. Volkov, And Andrey B. Evlyukhin

tldr: This paper studies biphoton generation via SPDC in a 3R-MoS2 van der Waals membrane metasurface, leveraging dual-resonant multipole resonances to enhance the generation rate.
motivation: Efficient biphoton sources are crucial for quantum technologies, and van der Waals materials offer a platform for compact, integrated nonlinear optics.
method: The authors design a double-membrane metasurface of 3R-MoS2 with two distinct hole arrays to support high-order multipole resonances, and model SPDC enhancement via dual-resonant excitation.
result: The metasurface design yields an increased SPDC photon generation rate compared to an unpatterned flake.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path toward on-chip biphoton sources using van der Waals materials, but the focus is on nonlinear optics and metasurface engineering rather than quantum information or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its approximation is classically hard, making it a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that includes state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots, showing that the algorithm runs with high fidelity on current hardware and scales favorably.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on lattice systems and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the relationship between space-time duality and quantum computation in many-body dynamics.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Realization Of Dissipation-Enhanced Topological Valley Transport In Phononic Crystal
authors: He Gao, Jiamin Guo, Yinjie Su, Zhongming Gu, Haoran Xue, And Jie Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): He Gao, Jiamin Guo, Yinjie Su, Zhongming Gu, Haoran Xue, and Jie Zhu

Dissipation, originating from intrinsic material absorption or leakage to the environment, is usually considered detrimental to wave transport. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a counterintuitive phenomenon where transport is enhanced by deliberately introduced dissipation in phononic crystal. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016301] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dissipation-enhanced topological valley transport in a phononic crystal, a counterintuitive phenomenon where added dissipation improves wave transport.
motivation: Dissipation is typically detrimental to wave transport; the authors aim to show that in certain topological systems, dissipation can actually enhance transport.
method: They experimentally realize a phononic crystal with designed dissipation and measure the valley transport properties.
result: They observe that dissipation enhances the topological valley transport, contrary to conventional expectations.
conclusion: Dissipation can be harnessed to improve transport in topological phononic systems, opening new possibilities for wave manipulation.

title: Embedding Independent Length Scale Of Flat Bands
authors: Seokju Lee, Seung Hun Lee, And Bohm-Jung Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Seokju Lee, Seung Hun Lee, and Bohm-Jung Yang

In flat-band systems with quenched kinetic energy, most of the conventional length scales related to the band dispersion become ineffectual. Although a few geometric length scales, such as the quantum metric length, can still be defined, because of their embedding dependence, i.e., the dependence on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016401] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an embedding-independent length scale for flat bands using the quantum metric, addressing a fundamental issue in flat-band geometry.
motivation: In flat-band systems, conventional length scales vanish, and existing geometric length scales depend on the embedding of the band, which is undesirable for a universal characterization.
method: The authors propose a new length scale derived from the quantum metric that is independent of the embedding, likely by considering the intrinsic geometry of the band.
result: They demonstrate that this embedding-independent length scale can be defined and computed for flat-band models.
conclusion: This work provides a robust geometric length scale for flat bands, which may be useful for understanding correlation effects and transport in such systems.

title: Direct Visualization Of Gate-Tunable Flat Bands In Twisted Double Bilayer Graphene
authors: Souvik Sasmal, Ryan Muzzio, Ahmed Khalifa, Paulina Majchrzak, Alfred J. H. Jones, I-Hsuan Kao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Simranjeet Singh, Eli Rotenberg, Aaron Bostwick, Chris Jozwiak, Søren Ulstrup, Shubhayu Chatterjee, And Jyoti Katoch
abstract:

The evolution of moiré minibands under varying carrier density and displacement field may be directly visualized using microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.

tldr: This paper experimentally visualizes gate-tunable flat bands in twisted double bilayer graphene using micro-focused ARPES.
motivation: Understanding the electronic structure of moiré materials is crucial for exploring correlated and topological phases, but direct visualization of band structure tuning has been challenging.
method: The authors use microfocused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (micro-ARPES) to directly image the evolution of moiré minibands as a function of carrier density and displacement field in twisted double bilayer graphene.
result: They observe gate-tunable flat bands and their evolution, providing direct evidence of band structure engineering in this moiré system.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a powerful technique for probing band structure in moiré materials, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Andreev Reflection To Probe Momentum-Dependent Spin Polarization In Altermagnet CrSb
authors: Yan Zhang, Yixuan Luo, Yue Yang, Zilong Li, Weilong Qiu, Lunhui Hu, Yuanfeng Xu, Yanfeng Guo, Chao Cao, And Xin Lu
abstract:

Altermagnetic materials have recently emerged as promising candidates for next-generation spintronic applications, characterized by the [MATH]-dependent spin-splitted band structure and a simultaneous zero-net-magnetization. Among them, altermagnetic candidate CrSb has attracted considerable a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016701] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies momentum-dependent spin polarization in altermagnet CrSb using Andreev reflection spectroscopy.
motivation: Altermagnets are promising for spintronics due to spin-split bands with zero net magnetization, and CrSb is a candidate material whose spin polarization properties need characterization.
method: The authors perform Andreev reflection measurements on CrSb to probe the momentum-dependent spin polarization of the electronic bands.
result: They observe clear signatures of spin polarization that depend on the crystallographic direction, confirming the altermagnetic nature of CrSb.
conclusion: Andreev reflection is an effective tool for probing spin polarization in altermagnets, and CrSb exhibits strong momentum-dependent spin splitting suitable for spintronic applications.

title: Orbital Altermagnetism In Two Dimensions
authors: Mingxiang Pan, Feng Liu, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingxiang Pan, Feng Liu, and Huaqing Huang

We introduce the concept of orbital altermagnetism, a symmetry-protected magnetic order of pure orbital degrees of freedom. It is characterized with ordered antiparallel orbital magnetic moments in real space but momentum-dependent orbital band splittings, analogous to spin altermagnetism. Using a m…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016702] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces orbital altermagnetism, a symmetry-protected magnetic order of pure orbital degrees of freedom in two dimensions.
motivation: To extend the concept of altermagnetism from spin to orbital degrees of freedom, exploring new magnetic phases.
method: Using a model Hamiltonian and symmetry analysis, the authors demonstrate orbital band splittings and antiparallel orbital moments.
result: They show that orbital altermagnetism exhibits momentum-dependent orbital band splittings analogous to spin altermagnetism.
conclusion: Orbital altermagnetism is a distinct magnetic phase that can exist in two-dimensional materials, with potential implications for spintronics and orbitronics.

title: Two-Band Superconductivity In Few-Layer ${\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{TaS}}_{2}$
authors: Shahar Simon, Maya Klang, Oded Millo, And Hadar Steinberg
abstract:

The nature of superconductivity in the transition metal dichalcogenide family, particularly [MATH] and [MATH] in the ultrathin limit, is not fully understood. While tunneling measurements apparently show a single superconducting gap,…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016001] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates two-band superconductivity in few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2 using tunneling spectroscopy.
motivation: The nature of superconductivity in ultrathin transition metal dichalcogenides is not fully understood, particularly the apparent single-gap behavior in tunneling measurements.
method: Tunneling spectroscopy measurements were performed on few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2 to probe the superconducting gap structure.
result: The measurements reveal two distinct superconducting gaps, indicating two-band superconductivity in these materials.
conclusion: The findings resolve the apparent discrepancy between tunneling and other measurements, confirming two-band superconductivity in few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2.

title: Landau Theory For Pair Density Modulation In Fe(Te,Se) Flakes

tldr: Develops a Landau theory for pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes based on STM experiments.
motivation: Recent STM experiments observed a pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes, and the authors aim to explain its physical origin using symmetry analysis.
method: The authors construct a Landau theory incorporating screw and glide symmetries to model the pair-density modulation.
result: The Landau theory successfully interprets the observed modulation in terms of symmetry-breaking and provides a framework for understanding similar phenomena.
conclusion: The pair-density modulation arises from symmetry considerations and can be described by a Landau theory, offering insights into the electronic properties of Fe(Te,Se).

title: High-$Q$ Nonlocal Resonances In Mirror-Enhanced Plasmonic Lattices
authors: Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, And Xianyu Ao

Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays stand as a versatile platform for enhancing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. Ultrahigh-quality-factor (high-[MATH]) resonances are critical for spectrally selective applications such as label-free biosensing, low-threshold lasing, and quantum information process…

tldr: This paper studies high-Q nonlocal resonances in mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices for enhancing light-matter interactions.
motivation: Ultrahigh-quality-factor resonances are critical for applications like biosensing, lasing, and quantum information processing, but achieving them in plasmonic arrays is challenging.
method: The authors propose a mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice design that supports nonlocal resonances with high Q-factors, analyzed through numerical simulations and theoretical modeling.
result: They demonstrate that the mirror configuration significantly boosts the Q-factor of nonlocal resonances, achieving values suitable for practical applications.
conclusion: Mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices provide a promising platform for high-Q resonances, with potential in nanophotonic devices and quantum information processing.

title: General-Purpose Inverse Design Of Heterogeneous Finite-Sized Assemblies
authors: Livia A. J. Guttieres, Ryan K. Krueger, Remi Drolet, And Michael P. Brenner

Designing heterogeneous, self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology. We present a framework that uses gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning systems toward target equilibrium yields. We design systems ranging from simple dimers to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018201] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a gradient-based optimization framework for inverse design of heterogeneous self-assembling systems to achieve target equilibrium yields.
motivation: Designing heterogeneous self-assembling systems is a central challenge in soft matter and biology, and existing methods lack general-purpose inverse design capabilities.
method: The authors use gradient-based optimization to invert an analytical yield calculation, tuning system parameters toward target equilibrium yields.
result: The framework is demonstrated on systems ranging from simple dimers to more complex assemblies, achieving target yields.
conclusion: The approach provides a general-purpose method for inverse design of heterogeneous finite-sized assemblies, with potential applications in soft matter and biology.

title: Nonreciprocity As A Generic Mechanism For Demixing In Flocking Mixtures
authors: Charlotte Myin And Benoît Mahault
abstract:

We show that even weak nonreciprocal alignment leads to large-scale structure formation in flocking mixtures. tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal alignment as a mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures, using simulations and continuum equations.
motivation: Understanding how nonreciprocal interactions affect collective behavior in active matter systems.
method: Numerical simulations of a binary Vicsek model and analysis of coarse-grained continuum equations.
result: Nonreciprocity destabilizes the ordered phase and leads to large-scale structure formation.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity is a generic mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures.
