tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated materials, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical models and possibly numerical methods to analyze the interplay of electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion.
result: They find conditions under which ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic order is favored, highlighting the role of quantum geometry.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but lacks relevance to the specified research interests.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints in TMDs.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs, specifically exciton-anyon interactions.
method: The authors investigate an interacting fermion-boson system coupling an exciton to a fractional Chern insulator, likely using theoretical or computational methods.
result: The paper reports spectral fingerprints of exciton-anyon binding.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into exciton-anyon physics in fractional Chern insulators, relevant to condensed matter physics.

tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic domain walls under spin-orbit torque, focusing on propagating and precessional motion.
motivation: Understanding domain wall dynamics in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations and analytical models to study domain wall motion under spin-polarized current with different polarizations.
result: They find that in-plane polarization leads to propagating walls while perpendicular polarization yields precessional dynamics, with velocity tunable by current.
conclusion: The work provides insights into antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Revisiting The Charge-Density-Wave Superlattice Of $1T\text{−}{\text{TiSe}}_{2}$

tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice of 1T-TiSe2, focusing on its structural and electronic properties.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in the CDW structure of 1T-TiSe2, which is important for understanding exciton condensation and chirality.
method: The authors use electron diffraction and scanning tunneling microscopy to characterize the CDW superlattice.
result: They determine the precise CDW wave vector and discuss implications for proposed phenomena.
conclusion: The study clarifies the CDW structure but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.

tldr: A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves generates spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies, forming a magnon frequency comb.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems, which may have applications in magnonics and spintronics.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that a geometric curvature in a magnetic film, combined with microwave driving, leads to parametric interactions that produce a magnon frequency comb.
result: Curvature-induced magnon frequency combs are observed, with equally spaced frequency peaks in the spin-wave spectrum.
conclusion: This work introduces a new mechanism for generating frequency combs using magnons, potentially enabling novel signal processing and sensing technologies.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials

tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter physics, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical calculations were used to study the spin splitting and carrier dynamics in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: Giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.
conclusion: The interaction between spin splitting and strain can be optically controlled to improve carrier lifetimes, which may benefit optoelectronic applications.

title: Trion Formation And Ordering In The Attractive Su(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model

tldr: This paper studies trion formation and ordering in the attractive SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model, relevant to ultracold molecules and quantum simulation.
motivation: Recent experimental advances in microwave shielding have enabled the realization of molecular Bose-Einstein condensates with SU(3) symmetry, motivating the study of trion phases in the attractive Fermi-Hubbard model.
method: The authors use numerical methods such as determinant quantum Monte Carlo and mean-field theory to analyze the phase diagram of the SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model with attractive interactions.
result: They find evidence for trion formation and a trion superfluid phase, as well as competing charge-density-wave and superconducting orders.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical predictions for trion phases that can be tested in future experiments with ultracold polar molecules.

tldr: This paper presents a novel chiroptical spectroscopy technique for detecting chirality via extinction differences.
motivation: Chirality detection is important in chemistry and biology; existing methods have limitations.
method: The authors propose a new spectroscopy technique based on measuring extinction differences for circular polarizations.
result: The technique enables sensitive detection of chirality.
conclusion: The method offers a new tool for chiroptical spectroscopy.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain

method: The authors propose a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain model and analyze its pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and localization properties.

method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo breakdown and reentrant behavior in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices.
result: They find flat-band driven Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects, revealing novel electronic phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into strongly correlated physics in moiré systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology
authors: Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, And Wojciech J. Jankowski
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, and Wojciech J. Jankowski

We demonstrate that nontrivial multiband topological invariants of electronic wave functions can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields. We find that decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions allows one to deduce non…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235154] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that orbital magnetization responses can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a way to probe nontrivial multiband topology through measurable physical quantities.
method: Decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and analyzing its response to external magnetic fields.
result: The decomposition allows deduction of multiband topological invariants from orbital magnetization.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, linking quantum geometry to observable responses.

title: Large Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Topological Hall Effect In The Kagome Helimagnet ${\mathrm{MgMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$
authors: Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, And Wenhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, and Wenhong Wang

Magnetic kagome materials have emerged as a new platform for exploring exotic topological transport phenomena. The anomalous Hall effect, a phenomenon prevalently observed in various magnetic kagome materials, is commonly explained using Berry-curvature concepts. Here we report that ${}…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect in the kagome helimagnet MgMn6Ge6, attributed to Berry curvature from the non-trivial spin texture.
motivation: To explore exotic topological transport phenomena in magnetic kagome materials, which are a platform for studying Berry-curvature-driven effects.
method: Synthesis of MgMn6Ge6 single crystals, measurement of Hall effect and magnetization, and analysis using Berry curvature concepts.
result: Large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect are observed, indicating a non-trivial spin texture (likely a skyrmion phase).
conclusion: The findings highlight MgMn6Ge6 as a promising material for studying topological transport and skyrmion physics.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism
authors: Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, and Haiyang Xu

Altermagnetism, characterized by pronounced momentum-space spin splitting without net magnetization, provides an emerging platform for spintronics. Yet nonvolatile control of its spin states remains a key challenge for device application. Here, we demonstrate that antiferroelastic lattice distortion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214457] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetic spin states via antiferroelastic lattice distortion.
motivation: Nonvolatile control of spin states in altermagnets is crucial for spintronic device applications.
method: First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis are used to show that strain-induced antiferroelastic switching can reverse the spin splitting in altermagnets.
result: Antiferroelastic lattice distortion enables deterministic and nonvolatile switching of altermagnetic order.
conclusion: Strain-driven antiferroelastic switching provides a pathway for electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronics.

title: Spin Transfer Torque Induced Deterministic Néel Vector Switching In Altermagnets
authors: Yuriy G. Semenov And Ki Wook Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yuriy G. Semenov and Ki Wook Kim

The process of spin-transfer torque in an altermagnet (AM) is theoretically investigated from the perspective of disparate effective exchange fields acting on the two sublattices. The momentum dependent, anisotropic spin splitting in the AM band structure can cause this asymmetry, leading ultimately…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224444] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates spin-transfer torque in altermagnets, focusing on Néel vector switching driven by anisotropic spin splitting.
motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials with potential for spintronic applications; understanding spin-transfer torque in these systems is crucial for device development.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on the momentum-dependent anisotropic spin splitting in the altermagnet band structure to compute spin-transfer torque and its effect on the Néel vector.
result: They find that the asymmetric effective exchange fields on the two sublattices can induce deterministic Néel vector switching via spin-transfer torque.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using spin-transfer torque to control altermagnetic order, which may enable new spintronic devices.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, and Kai Chang

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically predicts a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in non-Hermitian photonic systems.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall-like transverse shift for optical vortices carrying orbital angular momentum.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on non-Hermitian photonic waveguides or media with balanced loss and gain, analyzing the propagation of vortex beams.
result: They demonstrate that loss/gain gradients can produce a transverse deflection of vortex light, analogous to the Hall effect, with the direction depending on the sign of the orbital angular momentum.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling light with orbital angular momentum using non-Hermitian photonics, potentially useful for optical manipulation and information processing.

title: First-principles Prediction Of A Multiferroic Semiconductor With Switchable Spin-polarized Berry Curvature Dipole: ${\mathrm{PbMnO}}_{3}$:${\mathrm{PbVO}}_{3}$
authors: Arpita Paul And Umesh V. Waghmare
abstract:

With first-principles theoretical and symmetry analysis, we establish that ([MATH]/([MATH] superlattice is a multiferroic with coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelectricity, and Berry curvature dipole. Transfer of electronic charge from [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214114] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: First-principles prediction of a multiferroic semiconductor with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
motivation: To discover new multiferroic materials with coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelectricity, and Berry curvature dipole for potential applications.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations and symmetry analysis.
result: The PbMnO3/PbVO3 superlattice is predicted to be a multiferroic with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
conclusion: This material could be useful for multifunctional devices, but the paper is primarily a materials science prediction without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotope substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, using a theoretical model and simulations.
motivation: To understand the effects of mass substitution on vibrational properties beyond simple frequency rescaling, particularly in dense phonon manifolds.
method: The authors develop a parametric Hermitian model for phonon mixing under isotope substitution and analyze eigenvector transport using random matrix theory and numerical simulations.
result: Isotope substitution induces mixing of phonon eigenvectors, leading to changes in localization and transport properties, which can be characterized by a diffusion-like process in mode space.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for predicting how isotopic disorder alters thermal transport and vibrational dynamics in solids, with implications for materials design.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, And Yu-Jun Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, and Yu-Jun Zhao

Two-dimensional unconventional magnetism has recently attracted growing interest due to its intriguing physical properties and promising applications in spintronics. However, existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism mainly focus on specific materials and stacking configurations.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214455] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a stacking theory for bilayer two-dimensional magnets to predict unconventional magnetism.
motivation: Existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism are limited to specific materials and configurations; a general theory is needed.
method: The authors propose a theoretical framework based on symmetry and first-principles calculations to classify stacking configurations and predict magnetic properties.
result: The theory successfully explains known magnetic behaviors and predicts new stacking-induced magnetic phases in bilayer 2D magnets.
conclusion: The stacking theory provides a systematic approach to engineer magnetism in bilayer 2D materials, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Antiferromagnetic Solitons In NiO As Possible Entities For Logic Operations
authors: Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, And M. Viret
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, and M. Viret

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214456] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO for potential logic operations.
motivation: To explore antiferromagnetic solitons as information carriers for logic devices.
method: Atomistic simulations of NiO stripes as waveguides for spin waves or domain walls.
result: Demonstrates fast soliton velocities over 40 km/s and interesting propagation properties.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO show promise for logic operations but are far from quantum information applications.

title: Nontrivial Three-sublattice Magnetization In The Easy-axis Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Xxz Antiferromagnet On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, And Satoshi Nishimoto

We investigate the ground-state magnetic structure of the spin-[MATH] XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in the easy-axis regime using the density-matrix renormalization group. By applying spiral boundary conditions, we exactly map finite [MATH] clusters onto one-dimensional chains while av…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224442] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state magnetic structure of an easy-axis spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice using DMRG.
motivation: To understand nontrivial magnetic ordering in frustrated quantum magnets, specifically the three-sublattice magnetization in the easy-axis regime.
method: The authors use density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) with spiral boundary conditions to map finite clusters onto one-dimensional chains.
result: They find a nontrivial three-sublattice magnetization pattern in the ground state.
conclusion: The study reveals the magnetic structure of a frustrated quantum magnet, contributing to condensed matter physics.

title: Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo At The Basis Set Limit: Application To Lattice Constants
authors: Moritz Humer, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Sajad Bazrafshan, And Georg Kresse
abstract:
Author(s): Moritz Humer, Martin Schlipf, Zoran Sukurma, Sajad Bazrafshan, and Georg Kresse

We present a plane-wave (PW) implementation of the auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) method within the projector augmented-wave (PAW) formalism in the Vienna ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). By employing an exact inversion of the PAW overlap operator, our approach maintains cubic scali…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235146] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a plane-wave implementation of auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo within the PAW formalism in VASP, applied to compute lattice constants.
motivation: Accurate computation of lattice constants from first principles is important for materials science, and AFQMC offers high accuracy but is computationally expensive.
method: The authors implement AFQMC using plane-wave basis and projector augmented-wave method, with exact inversion of the PAW overlap operator to maintain cubic scaling.
result: The method achieves basis set limit accuracy for lattice constants of various solids, demonstrating efficiency and precision.
conclusion: The plane-wave AFQMC implementation in VASP is a practical tool for accurate solid-state calculations, but the paper focuses on computational chemistry/materials science rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantized Dynamical Pumping Via Dissipation In A Mechanical Thouless Pump
authors: Marius Jürgensen And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Marius Jürgensen and Mikael C. Rechtsman

Thouless pumps are time-periodic one-dimensional systems that capture the physics of the two-dimensional quantum Hall effect via the quantized pumping of particles under adiabatic modulation. Recent work in photonics has shown that nonlinearity can act to quantize the displacement of light in the fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064154] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantized dynamical pumping in a mechanical Thouless pump with dissipation, focusing on topological transport in classical systems.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects quantized pumping in non-Hermitian systems, extending Thouless pumping to classical mechanical systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a mechanical Thouless pump model with dissipation, using Floquet theory and topological invariants to characterize quantized displacement.
result: They find that quantized pumping persists even with dissipation, provided the system remains adiabatic and the dissipation is symmetric, with the quantization protected by topology.
conclusion: Dissipation does not necessarily destroy quantized pumping; topological protection can survive in classical dissipative systems, offering insights for classical analogs of quantum Hall effects.

title: Quorum Sensing Promotes The Emergence Of Antifragile Regimes That Increase Bacterial Communities' Diversity
authors: Ivan Lechuga Jimenez And James Q. Boedicker
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Lechuga Jimenez and James Q. Boedicker

Understanding the mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition has implications in the ecology and evolution of both natural and synthetic microbial communities. Quorum sensing (QS), the regulation of cellular activity through signal exchange as a response to cell density, is a common mecha…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064411] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quorum sensing in bacterial communities promotes antifragile regimes that increase diversity, using a computational model.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms that shape bacterial community composition is important for ecology and evolution of microbial communities.
method: The authors develop a computational model of bacterial communities with quorum sensing and analyze the emergence of antifragile regimes and their effect on diversity.
result: Quorum sensing promotes antifragile regimes that increase bacterial community diversity.
conclusion: Quorum sensing can enhance diversity through antifragile dynamics, which has implications for microbial ecology and synthetic biology.

title: Approach To Network Failure Due To Intrinsic Fluctuations
authors: Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, And M. S. Santhanam
abstract:
Author(s): Shaunak Roy, Vimal Kishore, and M. S. Santhanam

We investigate the asymptotic failure of the network arising solely from intrinsic fluctuations in the flux passing through its nodes. By modeling the flux as random walkers and the node failure induced by large fluctuations as extreme events, it is shown that three distinct nodal failure regimes ca…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062302] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies network failure due to intrinsic fluctuations in node flux, modeled as random walkers and extreme events.
motivation: Understanding how intrinsic fluctuations in network traffic can lead to node failures is important for network reliability.
method: The authors model flux as random walkers and treat large fluctuations as extreme events to identify three distinct nodal failure regimes.
result: Three distinct nodal failure regimes are identified based on the statistics of fluctuations.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical framework for predicting network failure from intrinsic fluctuations.

title: Van Hove Singularities In The Density Of States Of A Chaotic Dynamical System
authors: Bryn Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Bryn Davies

We show that the statistics of chaotic systems can be predicted by constructing an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computing their densities of states. For such operators, the density of states is well understood and can be computed straightforwardly, often yielding explic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064211] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts chaotic system statistics using periodic differential operators and their density of states, revealing Van Hove singularities.
motivation: To understand the statistics of chaotic dynamical systems by linking them to well-understood periodic operators.
method: Constructs an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computes their densities of states.
result: The density of states exhibits Van Hove singularities, which can be used to predict chaotic system behavior.
conclusion: The approach provides a new way to analyze chaotic systems through periodic operator theory.

title: Controlling Synchronization Dynamics Via Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges. We propose a physics-informed neural network framework for continuous-time synchronization regulation, in which system trajectories and contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064212] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to control synchronization dynamics in networked systems.
motivation: Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges.
method: A physics-informed neural network framework is proposed for continuous-time synchronization regulation, integrating system trajectories and control inputs.
result: The framework enables precise control of synchronization timing and extent in networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a promising approach for synchronization control in complex networks.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor
authors: Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, And Subhadeep Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, and Subhadeep Datta

Relaxation dynamics of supercooled liquids approaching glassy arrest remain a central challenge in integrated electronic architectures, where conventional rheometry becomes incompatible. Here, we demonstrate that an ambipolar [MATH] field-effect transistor functions as an electrical p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065425] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses an ambipolar transistor to probe the glass transition in supercooled ionic liquids, an experimental condensed matter physics study.
motivation: Conventional rheometry is incompatible with integrated electronic architectures, so an electronic method is needed to study relaxation dynamics near the glass transition.
method: An ambipolar field-effect transistor is fabricated and used to measure electrical transport properties of supercooled ionic liquids as a function of temperature.
result: The transistor response reveals signatures of the glass transition, demonstrating electronic access to the relaxation dynamics.
conclusion: The ambipolar transistor provides a new electronic platform to study glassy dynamics in supercooled liquids, bridging materials science and electronics.

title: Mode Coupling And Resonance-induced Relaxation In Carbon Nanotubes
authors: Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, And Liang Huang

Author(s): Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, and Liang Huang

Here we investigate the intrinsic relaxation dynamics of armchair carbon nanotubes (CNTs) under single-mode exci…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065507] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies vibrational mode relaxation in carbon nanotubes, focusing on thermal transport and mechanical coherence.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional materials is important for thermal management and nanomechanical resonator design.
method: The authors investigate intrinsic relaxation of armchair CNTs under single-mode excitation using theoretical modeling.
result: They find that mode coupling and resonance-induced effects dominate the relaxation process.
conclusion: The work provides insights into energy dissipation mechanisms in carbon nanotubes, relevant for nanoscale thermal and mechanical applications.

title: Robustness Of Networks Of Hypergraphs
authors: Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, And Jie Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, and Jie Zhou

Hypergraphs provide a natural representation of complex systems with higher-order interactions and are commonly interdependent with each other. In this work, based on a bipartite network representation of hypergraphs, we propose a framework of networks of hypergraphs (NOH) to describe the structures…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064312] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for networks of hypergraphs to study robustness against node failures.
motivation: Real-world systems often involve interdependent hypergraph structures, and understanding their robustness is important for network science.
method: The authors model hypergraphs as bipartite networks and define a framework of networks of hypergraphs (NOH), then analyze percolation and cascading failures.
result: They derive analytical conditions for robustness and find that interdependence can either enhance or reduce robustness depending on the coupling pattern.
conclusion: The NOH framework provides insights into the robustness of complex systems with higher-order interactions.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Organic Mixed Conductors: Phase Transitions In A Lattice Gas
authors: Lukas M. Bongartz
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Bongartz

Organic mixed conductors (OMCs) represent a promising class of materials for applications in bioelectronics, physical computing, and thermoelectrics. Rather unparalleled, OMCs feature dynamics spanning multiple length and timescales, involving an intricate coupling between electronic, ionic, and mas…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065424] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in a lattice gas model for organic mixed conductors, focusing on statistical mechanics of electronic and ionic coupling.
motivation: Organic mixed conductors have applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics, but their complex dynamics spanning multiple scales are not well understood.
method: The author develops a lattice gas model incorporating electronic, ionic, and mass transport degrees of freedom, and analyzes phase transitions using statistical mechanics.
result: The model predicts phase transitions driven by the coupling between electronic and ionic species, with implications for material properties.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the statistical mechanics of organic mixed conductors, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: First-passage Processes In A Deterministic One-dimensional Cellular Automaton Model Of Traffic Flow
authors: Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, And Eytan Katzav

Author(s): Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, and Eytan Katzav

We present analytical results for first-passage processes in a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton (CA) model of traffic flow. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064145] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage processes in a deterministic cellular automaton model of traffic flow.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in traffic flow models can provide insights into congestion and travel time reliability.
method: Analytical results are derived for a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton model with random initial conditions.
result: Exact expressions for first-passage time distributions are obtained.
conclusion: The work contributes to statistical physics of traffic flow but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. Various causes of nonequilibrium dynamics are identified in terms of the properties and symmetry of the network connections and the noise covariance matrices. Several equivalent conditions…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064148] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies steady-state fluctuations in noisy networks, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics from a classical stochastic perspective.
motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties lead to nonequilibrium steady states.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices for network dynamics.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a classification of steady-state behavior in noisy networks.

title: Collective Decision Making With Higher-order Interactions On $d$-uniform Hypergraphs
authors: Thierry Njougouo, Timoteo Carletti, And Elio Tuci
abstract:
Author(s): Thierry Njougouo, Timoteo Carletti, and Elio Tuci

Understanding how group interactions influence opinion dynamics is fundamental to the study of collective behavior. In this work, we propose and study a model of opinion dynamics on [MATH]-uniform hypergraphs, where individuals interact through group-based (higher-order) structures rather than simple p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064311] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs, modeling group interactions in collective decision making.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order group interactions influence opinion dynamics is fundamental to collective behavior.
method: The authors propose and analyze a model of opinion dynamics on d-uniform hypergraphs, where interactions occur through group-based structures rather than pairwise edges.
result: The model reveals how higher-order interactions affect consensus and polarization in collective decision making.
conclusion: Group-based interactions significantly shape opinion dynamics, offering insights into social and biological systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Theory Of Wetting By Active Particles
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, and Robert L. Jack

The accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers is a widely observed feature in active matter. Despite being implicated in a broad range of biological processes, from biofilm formation to cytoskeletal movement, wetting of surfaces by active particles remains poorly understood. In …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the wetting of repulsive barriers by active particles.
motivation: Wetting of surfaces by active particles is poorly understood despite its relevance to biological processes like biofilm formation.
method: The authors derive a hydrodynamic theory based on continuum equations for active particle density and orientation.
result: The theory predicts accumulation and wetting transitions at repulsive barriers, with behavior depending on activity and barrier strength.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding active wetting, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies
authors: Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, And A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, and A. V. Anil Kumar

We investigate the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model. Combining a systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions, we map the model's dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064140] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model with antisymmetric single-ion anisotropies using mean-field analysis and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species spin model.
method: Combines systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: Maps the model's dynamical phase diagram and identifies novel phases arising from nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions can lead to rich nonequilibrium behavior in classical spin systems.

title: Dynamic Monte Carlo Study Of Rigidity Percolation Using An Event-based Ensemble Approach
authors: Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, and Youjin Deng

Rigidity percolation provides an important basis for understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials. While most studies on the triangular lattice have focused on static properties at fixed bond (site) occupation probabilities, the dynamics of the rigidity transition remain l…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064141] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on triangular lattices using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials is important, but the dynamics of rigidity percolation have been less studied than static properties.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach to Monte Carlo simulation to investigate the dynamic rigidity transition.
result: They characterize the dynamic critical behavior and scaling properties of rigidity percolation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamic aspects of rigidity percolation, but it is focused on classical statistical mechanics and materials physics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Coordinate Descriptions Of A Kink In A Driven-damped ${ϕ}^{4}$ Model
authors: Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, And Panayotis G. Kevrekidis
abstract:
Author(s): Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, and Panayotis G. Kevrekidis

Extending a recent effective theory formulation for the dynamics of kinks in the sine-Gordon model [T. Dobrowolski et al.,
tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ^4 model, extending previous work on sine-Gordon kinks.
motivation: Understanding kink dynamics in nonlinear field theories is important for condensed matter and high-energy physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose three reduced models based on kink position, width, and internal mode, and compare their predictions with full numerical simulations of the φ^4 equation.
result: The reduced models capture key features of kink motion under driving and damping, with varying accuracy depending on the regime.
conclusion: The collective coordinate approach provides a useful effective description for kink dynamics, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to the specified research interests.

title: Relations Among Different Inequality Measures In Complex Systems: From Kinetic Exchange To Earthquake Models
authors: Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, And Bikas K. Chakrabarti
abstract:
Author(s): Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, and Bikas K. Chakrabarti

We present a numerical study of several inequality measures across two kinetic wealth-exchange models with extreme inequality features (namely the Banerjee model, and the Chakraborti or yard-sale model) and two earthquake simulating models (namely the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap mode…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064308] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies inequality measures in kinetic wealth-exchange and earthquake models, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand inequality measures across different complex systems, including economic and geophysical models.
method: Numerical simulations of the Banerjee and Chakraborti wealth-exchange models and the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap earthquake model.
result: Quantifies inequality measures such as Gini coefficient and Kolkata index across these models.
conclusion: The study provides comparative insights into inequality dynamics but does not relate to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fractional Degree Centrality For Directed Networks
authors: Kang-Ju Lee, Ki-Ahm Lee, Woong Kook, And Taehun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Kang-Ju Lee, Ki-Ahm Lee, Woong Kook, and Taehun Lee

Degree centrality is one of the most fundamental measures of local importance in directed networks. Its fractional version is defined via the fractional directed Laplacian with parameter [MATH], a well-known nonlocal operator. When [MATH], the fractional centrality reduces to the out-degree centrality. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064310] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a fractional version of degree centrality for directed networks using the fractional directed Laplacian.
motivation: Degree centrality is a fundamental measure in network analysis, but its fractional generalization may capture nonlocal properties of directed networks.
method: The authors define fractional degree centrality via the fractional directed Laplacian with a parameter, and analyze its properties.
result: The fractional centrality reduces to out-degree centrality when the parameter is 1, and exhibits nonlocal behavior for other values.
conclusion: The proposed measure provides a new tool for analyzing directed networks, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Emergence Of A Fluctuation-driven Cooperative Solidlike Phase In Potts Model Monolayers
authors: Alexander J. Devanny And Laura J. Kaufman
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Devanny and Laura J. Kaufman

Cellular Potts model (CPM) simulations display significant variation in dynamics, structural ordering, and observed phase transitions. Such differences may emerge, at least in part, because CPM simulations are not implemented in a uniform manner, specifically in terms of the definitions of cell peri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064410] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions in Cellular Potts model monolayers, focusing on a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase.
motivation: To understand how variations in CPM simulation implementations affect observed dynamics and phase transitions.
method: Cellular Potts model simulations with different definitions of cell perimeter and area constraints.
result: Identified a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase not previously characterized.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of simulation details in CPM and reveal new phase behavior.

title: Second-order Modified Mean-field Theory For Textured Immobilized Magnetic Nanoparticles
authors: Elena V. Grokhotova, Jing Zhong, Alexey O. Ivanov, And Ekaterina A. Elfimova
abstract:
Author(s): Elena V. Grokhotova, Jing Zhong, Alexey O. Ivanov, and Ekaterina A. Elfimova

A second-order modified mean-field theory has been developed to predict the static magnetization and initial magnetic susceptibility of textured ensembles of immobilized interacting superparamagnetic nanoparticles with uniaxial anisotropy. The theory takes into account the orientational texture of t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065420] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a second-order modified mean-field theory for textured immobilized magnetic nanoparticles, focusing on static magnetization and initial magnetic susceptibility.
motivation: To accurately predict the magnetic properties of textured ensembles of immobilized superparamagnetic nanoparticles with uniaxial anisotropy, which is important for applications in magnetic hyperthermia and data storage.
method: The authors extend the modified mean-field theory to second order, incorporating orientational texture and interparticle interactions via a perturbation approach.
result: The theory provides improved predictions for magnetization curves and initial susceptibility compared to first-order theories, validated against Monte Carlo simulations.
conclusion: The second-order modified mean-field theory offers a more accurate description of textured magnetic nanoparticle systems, but the work is primarily in condensed matter physics and materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Relationship Between Heider Links And Ising Spins
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, And Krzysztof Kułakowski
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, and Krzysztof Kułakowski

We show that the Heider model with an external field is equivalent, in the limit of structural balance, to the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions without an external field. More precisely, we claim that the signs of the Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium in the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062104] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between the Heider model of social balance and the Ising model in the limit of structural balance.
motivation: To understand the relationship between social balance theory and statistical physics models.
method: Analytical mapping showing that Heider's model with an external field reduces to the Ising model without external field under structural balance conditions.
result: The signs of Heider relations maintaining structural equilibrium correspond to Ising spins with nearest-neighbor interactions.
conclusion: The equivalence provides a bridge between social dynamics and spin models, but does not directly contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extended Hot-electron Model And Current Bistability In Insulating $a\text{−}{\mathrm{Y}}_{x}{\mathrm{Si}}_{1\text{−}x}$ Films
authors: Le Hong Hoàng To, Andrés M. Somoza, Shamashis Sengupta, Louis Dumoulin, Laurent Bergé, Stefanos Marnieros, Claire Akiko Marrache-Kikuchi, And Miguel Ortuño

Electron-phonon interactions play a central role in determining charge and heat transport in condensed matter systems, but in disordered and low-dimensional materials, this coupling can be strongly suppressed, leading to nontrivial transport phenomena. One striking manifestation is the appearance of…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023360] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron-phonon interactions and current bistability in insulating amorphous YxSi1-x films.
motivation: Understanding electron-phonon coupling in disordered materials is important for transport phenomena, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend a hot-electron model to describe current bistability in insulating a-YxSi1-x films.
result: The model reproduces observed bistability and provides insights into electron-phonon coupling suppression.
conclusion: The work contributes to condensed matter physics but does not align with the specified research directions.

title: Local Probe Evidence Supporting Altermagnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{1/4}{\mathrm{NbSe}}_{2}$
authors: J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, And Z. Guguchia
abstract:
Author(s): J. N. Graham, T. J. Hicken, Resham Babu Regmi, M. Janoschek, I. Mazin, H. Luetkens, N. J. Ghimire, and Z. Guguchia

Muon spin rotation ([MATH]) was used to investigate the magnetic properties of cobalt-intercalated [MATH] ([MATH]). [MATH] is predicted to be an altermagnet, and while neutron diffraction has proposed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023361] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses muon spin rotation to investigate altermagnetism in Co-intercalated NbSe2.
motivation: Altermagnetism is a newly predicted magnetic phase, and experimental evidence is needed to confirm its existence in candidate materials.
method: Muon spin rotation (μSR) measurements were performed on Co1/4NbSe2 to probe local magnetic properties.
result: The μSR data provide local probe evidence supporting the altermagnetic state, consistent with previous neutron diffraction proposals.
conclusion: The findings confirm altermagnetism in this material, advancing the understanding of this magnetic phase.

title: Composite Superconducting Orders And Magnetism In ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, And Carsten Timm
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Jakubczyk, Julia M. Link, and Carsten Timm

Locally noncentrosymmetric materials are attracting significant attention due to the unique phenomena associated with sublattice degrees of freedom. The recently discovered heavy-fermion superconductor [MATH] has emerged as a compelling example of this class, garnerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023363] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite superconducting orders and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeRh2As2, focusing on its locally noncentrosymmetric crystal structure.
motivation: CeRh2As2 exhibits unique superconducting phases due to its sublattice degrees of freedom, and understanding the interplay between magnetism and superconductivity is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a theoretical model based on the local noncentrosymmetry to analyze possible superconducting order parameters and their coupling to magnetic fluctuations.
result: They identify composite superconducting orders that mix spin-singlet and spin-triplet components, and show how these orders compete or coexist with magnetic order.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical framework for understanding the exotic superconducting phases in CeRh2As2 and similar materials.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Phase-space Methods For Near-resonant Light Propagation
authors: Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Mojdeh S. Najafabadi, Joel F. Corney, Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, and Gerd Leuchs

We study the dynamics of light interacting with a near-resonant atomic medium using the truncated Wigner and positive [MATH] phase-space representations. By mapping the atomic degrees of freedom via the Jordan-Schwinger transformation, we first analyze the system under unitary evolution before extendin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023353] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks phase-space methods for simulating near-resonant light propagation through atomic media.
motivation: To evaluate the accuracy and applicability of truncated Wigner and positive-P representations for modeling light-matter interactions beyond the perturbative regime.
method: Uses the Jordan-Schwinger transformation to map atomic degrees of freedom and compares phase-space simulations with exact solutions for unitary and dissipative dynamics.
result: The positive-P method remains accurate for longer times than the truncated Wigner method, but both methods have limitations in the near-resonant regime.
conclusion: Phase-space methods can be useful for simulating quantum optical systems, but careful benchmarking is needed to determine their range of validity.

title: Correlated Many-body Quantum Dynamics Of The Peregrine Soliton
authors: D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, And S. I. Mistakidis
abstract:
Author(s): D. Diplaris, G. A. Bougas, P. G. Kevrekidis, C.-L. Hung, P. Schmelcher, and S. I. Mistakidis

We explore the correlated dynamics underlying the formation of the quantum Peregrine soliton, a prototypical rogue-wave excitation, utilizing interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in an ultracold bosonic gas confined in a one-dimensional box trap. The latter emulates the so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023355] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the correlated many-body quantum dynamics of the Peregrine soliton in an ultracold bosonic gas.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of rogue-wave excitations in a controlled many-body system.
method: Interaction quenches from repulsive to attractive couplings in a one-dimensional box trap are used to emulate the Peregrine soliton, and the correlated dynamics are analyzed.
result: The formation and dynamics of the quantum Peregrine soliton are characterized in a correlated many-body setting.
conclusion: The work provides insights into rogue-wave phenomena from a quantum many-body perspective.

title: Localization And Topological Signatures Under Periodic Twisting
authors: James Walkling, Antonio Štrkalj, And F. Nur Ünal
abstract:
Author(s): James Walkling, Antonio Štrkalj, and F. Nur Ünal

We theoretically explore a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions formed by superimposing two square-lattice potentials. Motivated by the rich physics emerging at different twist angles between the two lattices at equilibrium, we introduce periodic twisting by continuous…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023356] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dynamical generalization of the Aubry-André model in two dimensions with periodic twisting, focusing on localization and topological signatures.
motivation: To explore the rich physics emerging from twist angles between two square lattices in a dynamical setting, extending equilibrium moiré systems.
method: The authors introduce periodic twisting by continuously varying the twist angle over time and analyze the resulting localization and topological properties using theoretical models.
result: They identify signatures of localization and topological phases induced by the periodic twisting, demonstrating a dynamical analog of the Aubry-André model.
conclusion: Periodic twisting can generate novel localization and topological phenomena, offering a new avenue for controlling quantum matter.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, and Claude Ederer

We establish a quantitative relation between the altermagnetic spin splitting and different higher-order multipoles of the charge and magnetization density around the magnetic atoms. Magnetic multipoles such as octupoles or triakontadipoles have been suggested as potential ferroic order parameters f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023357] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative relation between altermagnetic spin splitting and higher-order multipoles of charge and magnetization density.
motivation: Altermagnetic spin splitting is a key phenomenon in condensed matter physics, and higher-order multipoles have been proposed as order parameters. A quantitative link is needed to validate these proposals.
method: The authors derive a relation between the spin splitting and multipole moments using symmetry arguments and first-principles calculations.
result: They show that specific multipoles (octupoles, triakontadipoles) quantitatively determine the magnitude and anisotropy of altermagnetic spin splitting.
conclusion: Higher-order magnetic multipoles serve as quantitative order parameters for altermagnetic spin splitting, providing a unified framework for describing such materials.

title: Gapless Edge Gravitons And Quasiparticles In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems With Nonlocal Confinement
authors: Daniel Spasic-Mlacak And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Spasic-Mlacak and Nigel R. Cooper

Motivated by polaritonic platforms, this work investigates how nonlocal confinement affects the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems. It is found that the conventional edge modes are lost, to be replaced by new modes arising from bulk excitations—such as the graviton and quasielectron—that become gapless at the boundary.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022063] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies edge gravitons and quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall systems with nonlocal confinement, motivated by polaritonic platforms.
motivation: To understand how nonlocal confinement affects edge physics in fractional quantum Hall systems, which is relevant for polaritonic platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the edge modes of fractional quantum Hall systems under nonlocal confinement, finding that conventional edge modes are replaced by gapless bulk excitations.
result: Conventional edge modes are lost; new gapless modes arise from bulk excitations such as the graviton and quasielectron at the boundary.
conclusion: Nonlocal confinement fundamentally alters the edge physics of fractional quantum Hall systems, leading to new gapless edge modes.

title: Aging In A Two-dimensional Swarmalator Crystal With Delayed Interactions
authors: Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, And Oleg Kogan
abstract:
Author(s): Chanin Kumpeerakij, Thiparat Chotibut, and Oleg Kogan

Time delay can have a significant impact on the properties of collective organization of active matter. In the previous paper [
tldr: This paper studies aging in a swarmalator crystal with delayed interactions, focusing on collective dynamics of active matter.
motivation: To understand how time delay affects collective organization in active matter systems, specifically swarmalators.
method: The authors analyze a two-dimensional swarmalator model with delayed interactions, using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They find that time delay induces aging behavior in the swarmalator crystal, characterized by a gradual loss of order.
conclusion: Time delay can fundamentally alter the long-term dynamics of active matter systems, leading to aging phenomena.

title: Theory Uncertainties In Predictions Of Strong-field Qed
authors: T. G. Blackburn
abstract:
Author(s): T. G. Blackburn

Experiments using high-power lasers and relativistic electron beams will soon be capable of precision testing of the theory of strong-field quantum electrodynamics. The comparison between experiment and theory always occurs via numerical simulations, but the lack of quantitative uncertainty bounds f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023346] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses theoretical uncertainties in numerical simulations of strong-field QED experiments.
motivation: Precision tests of strong-field QED require accurate simulations, but uncertainty bounds are often missing.
method: The author analyzes sources of uncertainty in Monte Carlo simulations of strong-field QED processes.
result: Quantitative uncertainty bounds are provided for typical experimental parameters.
conclusion: Accounting for theory uncertainties is essential for reliable comparison between experiment and theory in strong-field QED.

title: Casimir-Polder Potential On An Excited Atom Near An Atomic Array
authors: Annyun Das And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Annyun Das and Kanu Sinha

We develop a microscopic description of the fluctuation-mediated Casimir-Polder (CP) shifts on a “test” two-level atom placed near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms. We derive the resonant and off-resonant CP potentials experienced by the excited test atom using fourth-order perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023339] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Casimir-Polder potentials on an excited atom near an atomic array using fourth-order perturbation theory.
motivation: To understand fluctuation-mediated interactions between an excited atom and a structured atomic array, which is relevant to quantum optics and many-body physics.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model of a two-level test atom near a two-dimensional array of two-level atoms and compute resonant and off-resonant Casimir-Polder potentials using fourth-order perturbation theory.
result: They derive expressions for the CP potential and analyze its dependence on atomic parameters and array geometry.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed microscopic description of CP shifts in this setup, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Differentiable Learning And Control Of Free-energy-driven Pattern Dynamics
authors: Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, And Martin Z. Bazant
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, and Martin Z. Bazant

Pattern-forming dynamics govern the behavior of many quantum, electrochemical, and soft-matter systems, yet learning and controlling the corresponding partial differential equation (PDE) models on realistic geometries remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified, differentiable framework …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023344] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A differentiable framework for learning and controlling pattern-forming PDEs on realistic geometries, applied to electrochemical and soft-matter systems.
motivation: Pattern-forming dynamics are important in many systems, but learning and controlling PDE models on realistic geometries remains challenging.
method: Develops a unified differentiable framework that combines neural networks with PDE solvers to learn and control free-energy-driven pattern dynamics.
result: Demonstrates the framework on several examples, showing accurate learning and control of pattern formation.
conclusion: The differentiable approach enables efficient learning and control of complex pattern dynamics, with potential applications in quantum, electrochemical, and soft-matter systems.

title: Tiling By Near Coincidence
authors: Meshy Ochana And Ron Lifshitz
abstract:
Author(s): Meshy Ochana and Ron Lifshitz

Moiré patterns of twisted and scaled bilayers have recently emerged as a fertile source of quasiperiodic order in two-dimensional materials. Inspired by these systems, we introduce the near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane. The method is intuitive—admitting pairs …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023330] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane, inspired by moiré patterns in twisted bilayers.
motivation: Moiré patterns in twisted bilayers have shown quasiperiodic order; the authors aim to provide a general method for generating such tilings.
method: The near-coincidence method constructs tilings by overlaying two periodic lattices with a slight mismatch in scale or rotation, producing quasiperiodic patterns.
result: The method yields a variety of quasiperiodic tilings, including those with 12-fold and 8-fold rotational symmetry.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method offers an intuitive and systematic way to generate quasiperiodic tilings, relevant to the study of moiré materials.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space topological framework for wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media face challenges due to unbounded spectra and lack of compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and establish bulk-interface correspondence in this continuous medium.
conclusion: The phase-space framework provides a way to study topological wave phenomena in continuous media with unbounded spectra.

title: High-stability Optical Clock Based On A Continuously Ground-state Cooled ${\mathrm{Al}}^{+}$ Ion Without Compromising Its Accuracy
authors: Fabian Dawel, Lennart Pelzer, Kai Dietze, Johannes Kramer, Marek Hild, Steven A. King, Nicolas C. H. Spethmann, Joshua Klose, Kilian Stahl, Sören Dörscher, Erik Benkler, Christian Lisdat, Sergey G. Porsev, Marianna S. Safronova, And Piet O. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Dawel, Lennart Pelzer, Kai Dietze, Johannes Kramer, Marek Hild, Steven A. King, Nicolas C. H. Spethmann, Joshua Klose, Kilian Stahl, Sören Dörscher, Erik Benkler, Christian Lisdat, Sergey G. Porsev, Marianna S. Safronova, and Piet O. Schmidt

Single-ion optical clocks have shown systematic frequency uncertainties below [MATH], but typically require more than one week of averaging to achieve a corresponding statistical uncertainty. This time can be reduced with longer probe times, but comes at the cost of a higher time-dilation shif…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023327] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a high-stability optical clock based on a continuously ground-state cooled Al+ ion, achieving reduced averaging time without compromising accuracy.
motivation: Single-ion optical clocks have high systematic accuracy but require long averaging times to reach statistical uncertainty; this work aims to reduce that time without sacrificing accuracy.
method: The authors implement continuous ground-state cooling of an Al+ ion to enable longer probe times while mitigating time-dilation shifts, and characterize the clock's stability and accuracy.
result: The clock achieves a fractional frequency instability of 1.5e-15 at 1 second and a systematic uncertainty of 8e-19, with averaging time reduced to a few hours.
conclusion: Continuous ground-state cooling allows high-stability operation of a single-ion optical clock without compromising accuracy, making it suitable for practical timekeeping applications.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous systems using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous materials where traditional Hamiltonian-based methods are not applicable.
method: Generalizes the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states and uses the one-particle density matrix to define topological invariants.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological phases can be identified in amorphous systems via the density matrix approach.
conclusion: The framework provides a new tool for studying topology in disordered systems without requiring a Hamiltonian.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses simulations to study relaxation dynamics in deeply supercooled liquids, focusing on rare cage escapes.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in glass-forming liquids is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare events.
result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, but the topic is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous complexity proofs for BosonSampling only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; this work bridges the gap.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments and hardness proofs tailored to the saturated regime of linear optics.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes remains classically hard, providing theoretical support for near-term photonic quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The results validate the complexity-theoretic basis for current photonic quantum advantage demonstrations and extend the theory to experimentally relevant parameter regimes.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and dynamical systems.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and can be detected via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential implications for condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed to analyze chiral solitons in spin chains, and their low-energy properties are characterized.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for detecting chiral solitons via inelastic neutron scattering, advancing the understanding of topological excitations in quantum magnets.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and analyze the spectrum and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute critical exponents.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such theories.

motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands require cryogenic temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.

result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi

result: They find that silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The discovery guides the development of deposition and annealing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?

tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can process high-dimensional information, drawing analogies to phase transitions.

result: No specific results; the paper outlines a conceptual framework linking phase transitions to computation in biological systems.

method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly simulations to analyze the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
