title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are an actively evolving field with expanding theoretical and experimental understanding.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on electronic states and many-body phenomena arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the exotic electronic states and responses in kagome metals, driven by frustration and interference effects.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and correlation effects.
result: Identifies unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and other emergent phenomena in kagome metals.
conclusion: Kagome metals host a rich variety of quantum states due to geometric frustration and electronic correlations.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents under a single field-theoretic framework.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, such as Doi-Peliti formalism and path integrals, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in reaction-diffusion processes.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unified tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic phases of matter that have been sought since the 1970s, and Kitaev's exactly solvable model provides a concrete platform to realize them in real materials.
method: The review summarizes theoretical developments of the Kitaev model and experimental progress in candidate materials, highlighting topological properties such as chiral edge modes.
result: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of Kitaev spin liquid research, including key materials and their properties.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with potential connections to topological quantum computation, but the review does not present new results.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity in the brain.
motivation: Understanding how coordinated activity in large neural networks underlies perception, thought, and action requires quantitative models bridging data and theory.
method: The authors review recent progress using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons simultaneously.
result: These statistical physics approaches uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can achieve predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for understanding neural network dynamics, but the paper is primarily a review of neuroscience applications rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: To understand and model the nonradiative relaxation process of internal conversion, which is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models and methods used to describe internal conversion, including quantum dynamics and nonadiabatic coupling approaches.
result: The review summarizes the current state of theoretical understanding and identifies key challenges and opportunities for incorporating these models into applied studies.
conclusion: Internal conversion is a complex process that requires advanced theoretical methods, and further development is needed to fully exploit it in practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored. This review aims to bridge the gap between classical skyrmion physics and quantum mechanics.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
result: It highlights that skyrmions can exhibit quantum behavior such as quantum depinning and may serve as qubits, but many quantum properties remain to be experimentally verified.
conclusion: Skyrmions offer a rich platform for studying topological quantum phenomena, but their integration into quantum information processing requires further research.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and to probe fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs current constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, and identifies promising avenues for future experiments.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a viable window into new physics, and ongoing experimental improvements will continue to tighten constraints or potentially discover new forces.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental limits, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where measured properties exceed classical bounds and identifies which assumptions are violated in each case.
result: It shows that apparent violations arise because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, homogeneity) used in deriving the bounds.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to deliberately violate these assumptions, enabling properties that surpass classical thermodynamic bounds.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for simulating quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body phenomena in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize in conventional settings, such as topology and gravity analogs.
method: The paper surveys various platforms (ultracold atoms, photonics, electronic systems) and techniques for engineering synthetic lattices with fractal, curved, or higher-dimensional geometries.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries, highlighting connections to condensed matter topology and cosmological models.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential to uncover new physics, but it remains largely exploratory and not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and its implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental observations, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Identifies that self-alignment fundamentally reshapes motion, enabling phenomena like orbiting and synchronized motion.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key property in active matter with broad applications, but the paper is a review without novel technical contributions to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and matter-wave interferometry.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity's quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence, collapse models, and entanglement mediation, alongside experimental platforms such as matter-wave interferometry and optomechanics.
result: Current experiments are approaching the regime where quantum effects of gravity could be observed, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, and ongoing experiments will guide future theoretical developments.

title: Quantum-Geometry-Induced Anomalous Chiral Transport And Hidden Symmetry Breaking In Centrosymmetric $2\mathrm{M}\text{−}{\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$
authors: Hang Cui, Shao-Bo Liu, Erqing Wang, Mingxiang Pan, Yuqiang Fang, Ning Ma, Wenlong Liu, Di Chen, Yu Zhang, Yuanjun Song, Tingting Hao, Jiankun Li, Jian Cui, Ya Feng, Haiwen Liu, Fuqiang Huang, Huaqing Huang, X.-C. Xie, And Jian-Hao Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Cui, Shao-Bo Liu, Erqing Wang, Mingxiang Pan, Yuqiang Fang, Ning Ma, Wenlong Liu, Di Chen, Yu Zhang, Yuanjun Song, Tingting Hao, Jiankun Li, Jian Cui, Ya Feng, Haiwen Liu, Fuqiang Huang, Huaqing Huang, X.-C. Xie, and Jian-Hao Chen

Chirality, a widely existing material property in nature that involves breaking the left-right symmetry, has had profound influence on various fields of natural sciences. Nonlinear responses, such as electronic magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA), have been recognized as sensitive probes for the effect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016302] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of quantum-geometry-induced anomalous chiral transport and hidden symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric 2M-WS2.
motivation: To explore chirality and nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric materials where conventional chiral effects are forbidden.
method: Experimental measurements of electronic magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA) and theoretical analysis linking it to quantum geometry (Berry curvature dipole).
result: Observation of large eMChA in centrosymmetric 2M-WS2, attributed to hidden symmetry breaking and quantum geometry effects.
conclusion: Quantum geometry can induce chiral transport even in centrosymmetric crystals, opening new avenues for nonlinear electronics.

title: Nonperturbative $S$-Matrix Renormalization
authors: Laurent Freidel, José Padua-Argüelles, Susanne Schander, And Marc Schiffer
abstract:
Author(s): Laurent Freidel, José Padua-Argüelles, Susanne Schander, and Marc Schiffer

We propose a renormalization group flow equation for a functional that generates [MATH]-matrix elements and which captures similarities to the well-known Wetterich and Polchinski equations. While the latter ones, respectively, involve the effective action and Schwinger functional, which are genuine off…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a renormalization group flow equation for generating S-matrix elements, analogous to Wetterich and Polchinski equations.
motivation: To develop a nonperturbative renormalization method directly for S-matrix elements, which are on-shell quantities, rather than off-shell effective actions.
method: The authors derive a functional flow equation for a generating functional of S-matrix elements, inspired by the Wetterich and Polchinski equations in quantum field theory.
result: They obtain a nonperturbative renormalization group equation that directly renormalizes S-matrix elements, capturing similarities to standard flow equations.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for nonperturbative studies in quantum field theory, potentially simplifying calculations of scattering amplitudes.

title: Geometric Representation Of Higher-order Optical Modes
authors: Claire Cisowski
abstract:
Author(s): Claire Cisowski

The author presents an octant geometric framework that maps higher-order, three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus. In contrast to standard Poincaré sphere analogs that are restricted to subspaces, this parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities where a mode amplitude vanishes.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063530] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric framework for representing higher-order optical modes on a sphere, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a complete geometric representation of higher-order optical modes beyond the standard Poincaré sphere.
method: The author develops an octant geometric framework mapping three-state optical modes onto a sphere spanned by a torus.
result: The parametrization covers the entire state space of structured light modes except for isolated coordinate singularities.
conclusion: The geometric representation offers a unified description of higher-order optical modes, but its relevance to the user's research interests is minimal.

title: Direct Measurement Of The $5s5p^{1}{P}_{1}→5s4d^{1}{D}_{2}$ Decay Rate In Strontium
authors: Naohiro Okamoto, Takatoshi Aoki, And Yoshio Torii
abstract:
Author(s): Naohiro Okamoto, Takatoshi Aoki, and Yoshio Torii

The authors experimentally measure the key transition parameters in neutral strontium directly. The measured branching ratio and decay rate differ substantially from previous theoretical predictions, motivating their reevaluation.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060803] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally measures the decay rate and branching ratio of a specific transition in neutral strontium, finding significant deviations from theoretical predictions.
motivation: Accurate atomic transition data are important for various applications, but previous theoretical calculations for this transition in strontium were uncertain.
method: The authors use laser spectroscopy to directly measure the 5s5p^1P_1 → 5s4d^1D_2 decay rate and branching ratio in a strontium atomic beam.
result: The measured decay rate and branching ratio differ substantially from earlier theoretical predictions, indicating a need for revised atomic models.
conclusion: The experimental results provide new benchmark data for strontium atomic structure, motivating reevaluation of theoretical calculations.

title: Probing Transition Rates, Nuclear Moments, And Electric Dipole Polarizability In Nobelium Using Multireference Fock-space Relativistic Coupled-cluster And Perturbed Relativistic Coupled-cluster Theories
authors: Ravi Kumar, Palki Gakkhar, D. Angom, And B. K. Mani
abstract:
Author(s): Ravi Kumar, Palki Gakkhar, D. Angom, and B. K. Mani

We employ an all-particle multireference Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster theory to compute the ionization potential, excitation energy, transition rate, and hyperfine structure constants associated with the $7{s}^{2}{{0ex}}}^{1}{S}_{0}→7s7p{{0ex}}}…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062815] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes atomic properties of nobelium using relativistic coupled-cluster theory.
motivation: To provide accurate theoretical predictions for transition rates, hyperfine constants, and polarizability of nobelium, which are important for atomic physics and precision measurements.
method: Employs multireference Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster and perturbed relativistic coupled-cluster theories to compute ionization potential, excitation energies, transition rates, and hyperfine structure constants.
result: Obtained numerical values for the ionization potential, excitation energies, transition rates, and hyperfine constants for nobelium.
conclusion: The computed results provide benchmark data for future experiments and improve understanding of atomic structure in heavy elements.

title: Structures And Proximity Effects Of Inhomogeneous Population-imbalanced Fermi Gases With Pairing Interactions
authors: Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, And Chih-Chun Chien
abstract:
Author(s): Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, and Chih-Chun Chien

By introducing spatially varying profiles of pairing interaction or spin polarization to quasi-one-dimensional two-component atomic Fermi gases confined in box potentials, we analyze the ground-state structures and properties when multiple phases coexist in real space by implementing the Bogoliubov–…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063324] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ground-state structures of inhomogeneous population-imbalanced Fermi gases with pairing interactions in quasi-one-dimensional box potentials.
motivation: To understand how spatially varying pairing interactions or spin polarization affect phase coexistence and structures in ultracold Fermi gases.
method: The authors implement the Bogoliubov–de Gennes formalism to analyze ground-state configurations of quasi-one-dimensional two-component atomic Fermi gases with spatially varying profiles.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases and analyze their properties, including proximity effects at phase boundaries.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the behavior of inhomogeneous Fermi gases, relevant to condensed matter and ultracold atom physics.

title: Resolution Of The Hyperfine Puzzle And Its Significance For Two-fermion Dirac Atoms
authors: Gordon Baym And Glennys R. Farrar
abstract:
Author(s): Gordon Baym and Glennys R. Farrar

If we could shrink the ground-state wave function of a hydrogen atom to a size [MATH], at fixed electron mass and charge, the singlet hyperfine attraction in a spin singlet state would scale as [MATH]—faster than the increase in kinetic energy—raising the question of why the hyperfine interaction …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062219] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves a puzzle in the hyperfine structure of two-fermion Dirac atoms, focusing on the scaling of hyperfine attraction in hydrogen-like systems.
motivation: The hyperfine interaction in a spin singlet state scales faster than kinetic energy when the wave function is shrunk, raising a fundamental question about the stability of such states.
method: The authors analyze the Dirac equation for two-fermion systems and compute the hyperfine splitting, accounting for relativistic effects and the finite size of the nucleus.
result: They resolve the hyperfine puzzle by showing that the apparent divergence is regularized by the finite size of the particles and relativistic corrections.
conclusion: The hyperfine interaction does not lead to instability, and the ground state remains bound, consistent with experimental observations.

title: Giant Field-free Transverse Josephson Diode Effect In Altermagnets
authors: Bijay Kumar Sahoo And Abhiram Soori
abstract:
Author(s): Bijay Kumar Sahoo and Abhiram Soori

We predict a field-free transverse Josephson diode effect in altermagnets (AMs) with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, achieving diode efficiencies exceeding [MATH] and unidirectional transverse supercurrents in four-terminal junctions. In this geometry, a longitudinal phase bias generates transverse sup…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245433] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts a field-free transverse Josephson diode effect in altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, achieving high diode efficiencies.
motivation: To explore the Josephson diode effect in altermagnets, which could enable new superconducting devices without external magnetic fields.
method: The authors theoretically model a four-terminal Josephson junction with altermagnet and Rashba spin-orbit coupling, calculating supercurrent and diode efficiency.
result: They find a field-free transverse Josephson diode effect with efficiencies exceeding 100% and unidirectional transverse supercurrents.
conclusion: Altermagnets with Rashba coupling can host a strong transverse Josephson diode effect, offering potential for superconducting electronics.

title: Predicting Interface And Spin States In Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Junctions
authors: Sofia Sanz And Daniel Sánchez-Portal
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Sanz and Daniel Sánchez-Portal

We present a theoretical analysis of interface states emerging at junctions between armchair graphene nanoribbons of varying widths. By exploring diverse width combinations and junction geometries, we demonstrate that predicting the precise number of interface states requires considerations beyond t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235434] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies interface states in armchair graphene nanoribbon junctions, focusing on electronic structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is important for nanoelectronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform theoretical analysis using tight-binding or DFT calculations to predict interface states for various width combinations and geometries.
result: They find that predicting the number of interface states requires considerations beyond simple width matching.
conclusion: The work provides guidelines for engineering interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions, but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Strongly Quenched Kramers Doublet Magnetism In ${\mathrm{SmMgAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, And Ross H. Colman
abstract:
Author(s): Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, and Ross H. Colman

We report magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on the rare-earth hexaaluminate [MATH], where [MATH] realizes a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice with an exceptionally weak net exchan…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224443] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental measurements of magnetic susceptibility, magnetization, and specific heat on a rare-earth hexaaluminate compound, revealing strongly quenched Kramers doublet magnetism on a triangular lattice.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of SmMgAl11O19, a rare-earth hexaaluminate with a triangular lattice, and characterize its low-temperature magnetism.
method: Magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements were performed on single crystals of SmMgAl11O19.
result: The compound exhibits a strongly quenched Kramers doublet with exceptionally weak net exchange interactions.
conclusion: The material provides a platform for studying frustrated magnetism in a triangular lattice with minimal exchange coupling.

title: Analytical Theory Of Chiral Active Particle Transport In A Fluctuating Density Field
authors: Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, And Shradha Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Jayam Joshi, Abhra Puitandy, and Shradha Mishra

We develop a closed-form analytical theory for the transport of a chiral active Brownian particle in three dimensions, moving through a fluctuating local density field that models steric and dynamical interactions in a dense active medium. The density field is modeled as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck proces…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064155] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical theory for chiral active particle transport in a fluctuating density field.
motivation: To understand transport of chiral active particles in dense active media, which is relevant to biological and soft matter systems.
method: Models the density field as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and derives closed-form expressions for transport coefficients.
result: Obtains analytical expressions for mean squared displacement and effective diffusion coefficient as functions of chirality and density fluctuations.
conclusion: The theory captures the interplay between chirality and environmental fluctuations, providing insights into active matter transport.

title: Stochastic Search With Space-dependent Diffusivity
authors: Hwai-Ray Tung And Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Hwai-Ray Tung and Sean D. Lawley

The canonical model of stochastic search tracks a randomly diffusing “searcher” until it finds a “target.” Owing to its many applications across science and engineering, this perennially popular problem has been thoroughly investigated in a variety of models. However, aside from some exactly solvabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064149] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic search with space-dependent diffusivity, a problem in statistical physics and applied mathematics.
motivation: Understanding how a diffusing searcher finds a target in heterogeneous environments is important for many applications, but exact solutions are rare.
method: The authors analyze a model where the diffusivity depends on the distance to the target, deriving exact expressions for mean first passage times and splitting probabilities.
result: They obtain closed-form results for certain diffusivity profiles, showing how spatial variations affect search efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into stochastic search in heterogeneous media, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Ballistic Motion Explains Fast Aggregation In Adhesive Active Matter
authors: Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, And Leonardo G. Brunnet
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, and Leonardo G. Brunnet

Inspired by motile cells in tissue formation, we find that active systems of self-aligning adhesive particles undergo ballistic aggregation through a flocking transition. This kinetic regime emerges when the cluster persistence length grows faster with cluster mass than the intercluster distance doe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065422] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ballistic aggregation in active matter systems, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Inspired by motile cells in tissue formation, the authors aim to understand fast aggregation in adhesive active matter.
method: They simulate active particles with self-alignment and adhesion, observing a flocking transition that leads to ballistic aggregation.
result: The cluster persistence length grows faster with cluster mass than intercluster distance, causing a kinetic regime of ballistic aggregation.
conclusion: The findings explain rapid aggregation in active systems but have no connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Elad Korngut and Michael Assaf

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction risk in assortative networks using stochastic simulations and analytical approximations.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in networks with assortative mixing.
method: The authors use a stochastic susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) model on assortative networks and derive analytical approximations for extinction probability, validated by Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They find that temporary lockdowns can either increase or decrease extinction risk depending on the timing and duration of the lockdown, and that assortativity significantly influences the outcome.
conclusion: Optimal lockdown strategies must consider network structure and timing to effectively reduce disease extinction risk.

title: Hydrodynamic Attraction And Hindered Diffusion Govern First-passage Times Of Swimming Microorganisms
authors: Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, And Christina Kurzthaler
abstract:
Author(s): Yanis Baouche, Magali Le Goff, Thomas Franosch, and Christina Kurzthaler

Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall reveal how hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion shape first-passage-time statistics. The results show that wall-induced hindered diffusion can strongly delay wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction produces distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022060] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near a wall using numerical simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic attraction and hindered diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how microorganisms encounter surfaces is important for biofilm formation and contamination, but the role of hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion is not fully understood.
method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion jointly govern first-passage times, with implications for microbial surface colonization.

title: Modulation Of High-energy Electrons With A Nanopore Matter Lens
authors: Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, And Changlin Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, and Changlin Zheng

We demonstrate the modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanosized pore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens. The inner Coulomb potential of matter decreases rapidly from the edge of the pore toward the center, creating a strong electric field on the order of 10 GV/m. This electric field st…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023345] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanopore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens.
motivation: To achieve strong focusing of high-energy electrons without the need for bulky magnetic lenses, enabling compact electron optics.
method: The authors use a nanosized pore in a solid material, where the inner Coulomb potential creates a strong electric field (∼10 GV/m) to focus electrons.
result: They show that the nanopore acts as an effective electrostatic lens for high-energy electrons, achieving modulation and focusing.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a new approach for electron beam manipulation, potentially useful in electron microscopy and lithography.

title: Stochastic Acceleration Of Electrons In Fluctuating Fields Induced By Stimulated Raman Scattering In Subrelativistic Laser-plasma Interactions
authors: Yuji Takagi, Natsumi Iwata, Emmanuel D’humieres, Takayoshi Sano, And Yasuhiko Sentoku
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Takagi, Natsumi Iwata, Emmanuel d’Humieres, Takayoshi Sano, and Yasuhiko Sentoku

authors: Karan K. H. Manjunatha, Joakim Vianney Ngamsa Tegnitsap, Manyu Zhao, Lucia Valentina Gambuzza, Yafang Dong, Wei Zhang, Pedro Antonio Valdes-Sosa, Stefano Boccaletti, Mattia Frasca, And Ludovico Minati

method: A network of 59 coupled chaotic electronic oscillators modeled after a dissociated rat cortical culture was built, and a spectral block method was used to predict cluster synchronization.
result: Cluster synchronization was observed experimentally, validating the spectral block prediction method.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that cluster synchronization can be predicted and observed in complex neuronal-like networks, which may have implications for neuroscience and network theory.

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can be used as cryptographic primitives by analyzing their collision resistance.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, likely using theoretical complexity arguments and algorithmic analysis.
result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions in the studied neural network model.
conclusion: The result suggests potential for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models, but the paper is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe

motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under varying electric and magnetic fields.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders is demonstrated.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall states and magnetic phase transitions, with potential for future quantum devices.

tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in two-dimensional photonic crystals with stealthy hyperuniform disorder, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show unexpected scattering that needs explanation.

result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of radiative loss in disordered photonic materials, impacting their optical properties.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics

abstract:

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in both optical and acoustic wave fields.
result: They show that the same physical principles govern forces and torques in optics and acoustics, enabling cross-disciplinary insights.
conclusion: The unified perspective can guide future developments in particle manipulation using light and sound.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses gravitational wave signals from the early universe, including phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves provide a unique probe of the first second of the universe, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical predictions for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from cosmological sources and detection strategies.
result: It summarizes possible signals from phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe phenomena.
conclusion: Gravitational wave astronomy can reveal physics of the early universe that is otherwise inaccessible.

authors: Ayush Roy, Lorenzo Küchler, Adam Pound, And Rodrigo Panosso Macedo
abstract:

A modular framework within the self-force formalism that applies to a large class of effective field theories of gravity in order to perform tests of general relativity with binary black hole mergers is critical for tests of general relativity that make use of the upcoming space-based gravitational wave detectors such as LISA.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251404] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a self-force framework for black hole mergers in modified gravity theories, aimed at testing general relativity with LISA.
motivation: To enable tests of general relativity using gravitational wave observations from LISA, a modular self-force formalism is needed for binary black hole mergers in effective field theories of gravity.
method: The authors construct a self-force approach within a large class of effective field theories, extending the standard self-force formalism to include modifications to general relativity.
result: They present a modular framework that can compute gravitational waveforms for black hole mergers in modified gravity, applicable to future space-based detectors.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical tool for testing general relativity with LISA, but it is primarily a gravitational physics result with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper develops extended mean-field theories to model activity patterns in networks of real biological neurons.
motivation: Understanding collective activity in biological neural networks is challenging due to complex interactions; mean-field approximations offer a tractable approach.
method: The authors propose extended mean-field theories that go beyond standard approximations to capture correlations and heterogeneity in neuronal networks.
result: The extended mean-field theories accurately reproduce activity patterns observed in experimental data from biological neurons.
conclusion: Extended mean-field theories provide a powerful tool for modeling real neural networks, bridging theory and experiment in neuroscience.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256402] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the size and dynamics of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium using inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding electron correlations in materials is fundamental to condensed matter physics, and the dynamic behavior of the exchange-correlation hole is not well characterized.
method: The authors use inelastic X-ray scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor of beryllium and extract the real-space exchange-correlation hole as a function of energy transfer.
result: The exchange-correlation hole size is about 2 Å at low energy, but extends to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, indicating strong dynamic effects.
conclusion: Electron correlations in beryllium are significantly influenced by electron dynamics, which must be accounted for in theoretical models.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties constrain the behavior of matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements provide constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state and our understanding of dense matter.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond Standard Model physics, and the HL-LHC offers a new opportunity to discover it.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels.
result: Stringent bounds have been placed on supersymmetric parameter space, but several well-motivated scenarios remain viable for HL-LHC exploration.
conclusion: The HL-LHC has significant potential to discover or further constrain supersymmetry, guiding future model building.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and diagnostics.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: It summarizes updated nuclear reaction data and improved solar models that better match neutrino and helioseismic observations.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers three real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review techniques that provide direct real-space access.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can reveal atomic-scale disorder and defects in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods are powerful for characterizing disorder, and combining them yields more comprehensive insights.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but many reactions have very small rates and are difficult to measure directly.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions on Earth.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of the current theoretical understanding and experimental challenges in low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand the quantum physics underlying stellar nuclear reactions.

result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The updated CODATA values serve as the internationally accepted reference for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical calculations.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to visualize cells and tissues.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic signal generation, detection, and multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy can image millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing unique optical contrast in biological tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical research, with ongoing developments in multimodal imaging.

authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.

motivation: Understanding creases and cusps in biological and materials contexts requires nonlinear elasticity beyond linear buckling analysis.

result: Provides a modern treatment of surface instabilities in growing soft solids.

authors: J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, And X. Z. Zhang

conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical improvement for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023333] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the higher Curie temperature of Fe3GaTe2 compared to Fe3GeTe2 using magnetic exchange interaction theory.
motivation: Understanding why Fe3GaTe2 has a higher Curie temperature than Fe3GeTe2 is important for developing two-dimensional magnetic materials with potential spintronic applications.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations based on density functional theory to compute magnetic exchange interactions and estimate Curie temperatures.
result: They find that the stronger in-plane magnetic anisotropy and larger exchange coupling in Fe3GaTe2 lead to its higher Curie temperature.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical explanation for the enhanced Curie temperature in Fe3GaTe2, which may guide the design of high-temperature two-dimensional magnets.

result: A local density peak forms near the magnetic nozzle throat, indicating that ambipolar electric fields enhance plasma production remotely.
conclusion: Ambipolar electric fields in convergent magnetic fields can be used for remote plasma production, relevant to electric propulsion and plasma processing.

result: The work reveals the multiscale nature of soft solid interfaces, providing insights into their mechanical behavior.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the fundamental understanding of soft solid mechanics but are unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and demonstrates its application to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications, breaking the traditional bandwidth limit of resonant modes.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei

tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue in soft materials is important for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and connect to bulk hydrogel behavior.
result: A force-response model is developed that explains fatigue behavior and provides design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work offers insights into fatigue fracture in soft materials and a design principle for improving hydrogel durability.
